sentences.zh: 王俊，城武人。

translations.literal: Wang Jun was a man of Chengwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was a native of Chengwu.

sentences.zh: 父為順天府知事。

translations.literal: His father served as secretary of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father held the post of secretary in Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 母卒於官舍，俊扶櫬還葬，刈草萊為茇舍，寢處塋側。

translations.literal: His mother died at the official residence; Jun shouldered the coffin home for burial, cut wild grass to make a thatched hut, and slept beside the grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died at the official residence, Jun carried the coffin home for burial, cut wild grass to build a mourning hut, and slept beside the grave.

sentences.zh: 野火延巘將及，俊叩首慟哭，火及塋樹而止。

translations.literal: A wildfire spread along the hill and was about to reach the grave; Jun kowtowed and wailed bitterly, and when the fire reached the trees of the grave mound it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A wildfire crept along the hillside toward the grave; Jun kowtowed and wept until the flames reached the trees on the mound and then died out.

sentences.zh: 正統三年被旌。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong he received imperial commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhengtong reign he was officially commended.

sentences.zh: 劉準者，唐山諸生。

translations.literal: Liu Zhun was a student of Tangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhun was a licentiate of Tangshan.

sentences.zh: 父喪，廬墓。

translations.literal: When his father died, he dwelt in a hut by the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his father's death he lived in a mourning hut beside the grave.

sentences.zh: 冬月野火將及冢樹，準悲號告天，火遂息。

translations.literal: In winter a wildfire was about to reach the trees on the tomb; Zhun wailed to Heaven in grief, and the fire then died out.
translations.idiomatic: One winter a wildfire threatened the trees on the grave; Zhun cried out to Heaven in grief, and the fire went out.

sentences.zh: 正統六年旌表。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong he was officially commended.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhengtong reign he received an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 楊敬者，歸德人。

translations.literal: Yang Jing was a man of Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jing was a native of Guide.

sentences.zh: 父歿於陣，為木主招魂以葬。

translations.literal: His father died in battle; he made a wooden spirit tablet to summon the soul and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: His father fell in battle; he fashioned a wooden spirit tablet to recall his soul and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 每讀書至戰陣之事，輒隕涕不止。

translations.literal: Whenever he read of battle and warfare, tears would fall without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his reading touched on battle and warfare, he wept without end.

sentences.zh: 母歿，柩在堂。

translations.literal: When his mother died, the coffin lay in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, her coffin remained in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 鄰家失火，烈焰甚迫，敬撫柩哀號，風止火滅。

translations.literal: A neighbor's house caught fire and fierce flames pressed close; Jing embraced the coffin and wailed, and the wind ceased and the fire died.
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor's house caught fire and the flames drew near, Jing clung to the coffin and wailed; the wind dropped and the fire went out.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年旌表。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he was officially commended.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Zhengtong reign he received an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 石鼐，渾源諸生。

translations.literal: Shi Nai was a student of Hunyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Nai was a licentiate of Hunyuan.

sentences.zh: 父歿，廬墓。

translations.literal: When his father died, he dwelt in a hut by the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his father's death he lived in a mourning hut beside the grave.

sentences.zh: 墓初成，天大雨，山水驟漲。

translations.literal: When the tomb was newly finished, Heaven sent great rain and mountain waters suddenly rose.
translations.idiomatic: The grave had only just been completed when heavy rains fell and mountain floods surged.

sentences.zh: 鼐仰天號哭，水將及墓，忽分兩道去，墓獲全。

translations.literal: Nai cried to Heaven; the water was about to reach the tomb when it suddenly split in two courses and passed by, and the tomb was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Nai looked up and wailed; as the flood was about to reach the grave, the waters suddenly divided in two and flowed around it, leaving the tomb intact.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年旌表。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi he was officially commended.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Hongzhi reign he received an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 任鏜，夏邑人。

translations.literal: Ren Tang was a man of Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Tang was a native of Xiayi.

sentences.zh: 嫡母卒，廬於墓。

translations.literal: When his legal mother died, he dwelt at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When his legal mother died, he lived in a mourning hut at her grave.

sentences.zh: 黃河沖溢，將嚙塋域。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst its banks and was about to gnaw away the grave precinct.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River overflowed and threatened to erode the burial ground.

sentences.zh: 鏜伏地號哭，河即南徙。

translations.literal: Tang prostrated himself on the ground and wailed; the river at once shifted southward.
translations.idiomatic: Tang threw himself to the ground and wailed, and the river immediately shifted its course to the south.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十五年旌表。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Jiajing he was officially commended.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of the Jiajing reign he received an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 史五常，內黃人。

translations.literal: Shi Wuchang was a man of Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wuchang was a native of Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 父萱，官廣東僉事。

translations.literal: His father Xuan held office as surveillance commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan served as surveillance commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 卒，葬南海和光寺側。

translations.literal: He died and was buried beside Heguang Temple in Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was buried beside Heguang Temple in Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 五常方七歲，母攜以歸。

translations.literal: Wuchang was just seven; his mother took him and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang was only seven years old when his mother brought him home.

sentences.zh: 比長，奉母至孝，常恨父不得歸葬。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he served his mother with utmost filial piety and constantly grieved that his father could not be brought home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he cared for his mother with deep devotion and always regretted that his father had never been brought home for burial.

sentences.zh: 母語之曰：「爾父杉木櫬內，置大錢十，爾謹誌之。

translations.literal: His mother told him, "Inside your father's fir-wood coffin are placed ten large coins—remember this well.
translations.idiomatic: His mother told him, "Inside your father's fir coffin are ten large coins—keep that firmly in mind.

sentences.zh: 」母歿，廬墓致毀，既終喪，往迎父櫬。

translations.literal: " When his mother died, he dwelt by the tomb in such grief that his body wasted away; when mourning was finished, he went to fetch his father's coffin.
translations.idiomatic: " After his mother died he kept vigil at her grave until he was emaciated with grief; when the mourning period ended, he set out to bring his father's coffin home.

sentences.zh: 時相去已五十年，寺沒於水久矣。

translations.literal: By then fifty years had passed, and the temple had long been submerged in water.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty years had already passed, and the temple had long lain beneath the water.

sentences.zh: 五常泣禱，有老人以杖指示寺址。

translations.literal: Wuchang wept and prayed; an old man pointed out the site of the temple with his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang wept and prayed, and an old man indicated the temple's location with his staff.

sentences.zh: 發地，果得父櫬，內置錢如母言，乃扶歸，與母合葬，復廬墓側。

translations.literal: They dug into the ground and indeed found his father's coffin; inside were coins as his mother had said. He then shouldered it home, buried father and mother together, and again dwelt beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: They excavated the site and found his father's coffin, with the coins inside exactly as his mother had described. He carried it home, buried his parents together, and once more lived in a hut beside the grave.

sentences.zh: 正統六年旌表。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong he was officially commended.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhengtong reign he received an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 周敖，河州衛軍家子也。

translations.literal: Zhou Ao was the son of a military household of Hezhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ao was the son of a soldier's family registered at Hezhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 正統末，聞英宗北狩，大哭，不食七日而死。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengtong, hearing that Emperor Yingzong had been taken north on campaign, he wept greatly, ate nothing for seven days, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhengtong reign, when he heard that Emperor Yingzong had been captured on the northern campaign, he wept bitterly, refused food for seven days, and died.

sentences.zh: 其子諸生路方讀書別墅，聞父死，慟哭奔歸，以頭觸庭槐亦死。

translations.literal: His son, the student Lu, was reading at a country villa; hearing of his father's death, he wailed and ran home, struck his head against the courtyard locust tree, and also died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lu, a licentiate, was studying at a country retreat; when he learned of his father's death he rushed home weeping, dashed his head against the locust in the courtyard, and died as well.

sentences.zh: 鄉人異之，聞於州。

translations.literal: The villagers marveled at this and reported it to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers were astonished and reported the matter to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知州躬臨其喪，賻麥四十斛、白金一斤。

translations.literal: The prefect came in person to their funeral and gave condolence gifts of forty hu of wheat and one jin of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect attended the funerals in person and sent forty hu of wheat and one jin of silver as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 路妻方氏，厲誌守節，撫子堂成立，後為知縣。

translations.literal: Lu's wife, the Lady Fang, resolved to preserve her chastity, reared her son Tang to maturity, and he later became district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's wife Lady Fang held firmly to her widowhood, raised their son Tang to adulthood, and he later became a district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 鄭韺，石康人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yin was a man of Shikang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yin was a native of Shikang.

sentences.zh: 父賜，舉人，兄頀，進士。

translations.literal: His father Ci was a provincial graduate; his elder brother Hao was a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ci was a provincial graduate, and his elder brother Hao a metropolitan graduate.

sentences.zh: 天順中，母為瑤賊所掠。

translations.literal: During Tianshun his mother was seized by Yao bandits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshun reign his mother was carried off by Yao bandits.

sentences.zh: 韺年十六，挺身入賊壘，紿之曰：「吾欲丐吾母，豈惜金，第金皆母所瘞，願代母歸取之。

translations.literal: Yin was sixteen; he entered the bandit camp bodily and deceived them, saying, "I wish to beg for my mother—would I begrudge gold? Only the gold was all buried by my mother; let me go back in her place to fetch it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was sixteen. He went alone into the bandits' camp and told them, "I have come to ransom my mother—I would not begrudge gold. But the gold was all buried by my mother; let me return in her place to dig it up.

sentences.zh: 」賊遂拘韺而釋母，然其家實無金也，韺遂被殺。

translations.literal: " The bandits then detained Yin and released his mother, but the family in truth had no gold, and Yin was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: " The bandits held Yin and released his mother, but the family in fact had no gold, and Yin was killed.

sentences.zh: 廉州知府張嶽建祠祀之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue, prefect of Lianzhou, built a shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue, prefect of Lianzhou, erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 榮瑄，瓊州人。

translations.literal: Rong Xuan was a man of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Xuan was a native of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 三歲而孤，與兄琇並以孝聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned at three, he and his elder brother Xiu were both famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at the age of three, he and his elder brother Xiu were both renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 天順四年，土賊據瓊城，瑄兄弟扶母走避。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun, native bandits held Qiong city; the Xuan brothers supported their mother and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianshun, local rebels seized Qiong city, and the brothers fled with their mother.

sentences.zh: 遇賊，琇謂瑄曰：「我以死衛母，汝急去。

translations.literal: They met the bandits; Xiu said to Xuan, "I will die to defend our mother—you flee at once.
translations.idiomatic: They encountered the rebels, and Xiu said to Xuan, "I will die defending our mother—you must run.

sentences.zh: 」瑄從之，琇與母遂陷賊中。

translations.literal: " Xuan obeyed; Xiu and their mother then fell into the bandits' hands.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan fled as told, and Xiu and their mother were taken by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 官軍至，琇被執。

translations.literal: When government troops arrived, Xiu was seized.
translations.idiomatic: When government troops arrived, Xiu was captured.

sentences.zh: 主將將殺琇，瑄趨至，叩頭流血，泣請曰：「兄以母故陷賊，母老家貧，恃兄為命，願殺瑄存兄養母。

translations.literal: The commander was about to execute Xiu; Xuan hurried up, kowtowed until blood flowed, and weeping begged, saying, "My brother fell into the bandits' hands on our mother's account; our mother is old and our family poor and depends on my brother for her life—I beg you kill Xuan and spare my brother to support our mother.
translations.idiomatic: The commander was about to execute Xiu when Xuan rushed forward, kowtowed until his forehead bled, and pleaded through tears, "My brother was captured because of our mother; she is old and our family is poor and relies on him for her livelihood. Kill me instead and let my brother live to care for her.

sentences.zh: 」主將不察，竟殺瑄。

translations.literal: " The commander did not investigate and in the end killed Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: " The commander paid no heed and executed Xuan instead.

sentences.zh: 後有葉文榮，海寧人。

translations.literal: Later there was Ye Wenrong, a man of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was Ye Wenrong of Haining.

sentences.zh: 弟殺人論死，母日悲泣不食。

translations.literal: His younger brother killed a man and was sentenced to death; their mother daily wept in grief and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother had killed a man and was condemned to death; day after day their mother wept and refused food.

sentences.zh: 文榮謂母曰：「兒年已長，有子，請代弟死。

translations.literal: Wenrong said to his mother, "Your son is already grown and has a child; I beg to die in my brother's place.
translations.idiomatic: Wenrong told his mother, "I am grown and have a son of my own—let me die in my brother's stead.

sentences.zh: 」遂詣官服殺人罪，弟得釋，而文榮坐死。

translations.literal: " He then went to the authorities and confessed to murder; his brother was released, while Wenrong was executed.
translations.idiomatic: " He went to the magistrate and confessed to the killing; his brother was freed, and Wenrong was put to death.

sentences.zh: 傅檝，字定濟，泉州南安人。

translations.literal: Fu Ji, style name Dingji, was a man of Nan'an in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ji, styled Dingji, was a native of Nan'an in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖凱，父浚，並進士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kai and father Jun were both metropolitan graduates.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kai and his father Jun had both passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 為部郎。

translations.literal: He served as a department secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Jun served as a secretary in a ministry.

sentences.zh: 檝年十六舉鄉試，二十成進士。

translations.literal: Ji at sixteen passed the provincial examination and at twenty became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Ji passed the provincial examination at sixteen and the metropolitan examination at twenty.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，授行人，出行襄府。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi he was appointed courier and traveled on mission to the Xiang princedom.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign he was appointed a courier and sent on embassy to the Xiang princedom.

sentences.zh: 半道聞母病，請入京省視再往竣事。

translations.literal: Halfway he heard his mother was ill and asked to enter the capital to visit her before completing his mission.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway he learned his mother was ill and asked leave to visit her in the capital before finishing his errand.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書劉春曰：「無害於若，而可教孝。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Liu Chun said, "It does no harm to you and can teach filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Liu Chun said, "This will do you no harm and sets an example of filial duty.

sentences.zh: 」奏許之。

translations.literal: " He memorialized and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized the throne, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 浚後遷山東鹽運司同知。

translations.literal: Jun was later transferred to be assistant commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was later promoted to assistant commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 娶繼妻，私其二奴。

translations.literal: He took a stepwife who secretly kept two male slaves.
translations.idiomatic: He remarried, and his new wife secretly took two male servants as lovers.

sentences.zh: 浚聞將治之，遂暴卒。

translations.literal: Jun heard of it and was about to punish them, whereupon he suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun learned of this and was about to punish them, he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 檝心疑未發，奴遽亡去。

translations.literal: Ji suspected this in his heart but had not yet acted when the slaves fled at once.
translations.idiomatic: Ji harbored suspicions but had not yet acted when the slaves fled.

sentences.zh: 久之，偵一奴逃德化縣，傭巨姓家。

translations.literal: After a long time he tracked one slave who had fled to Dehua County and was hired by a great clan.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he traced one slave to Dehua County, where he was working as a hired hand for a wealthy family.

sentences.zh: 檝微行往伺奴出，袖鐵椎擊殺之，而其一不可跡矣。

translations.literal: Ji went in disguise to watch for the slave's coming out, struck and killed him with an iron mallet hidden in his sleeve, while the other could not be traced.
translations.idiomatic: Ji went in disguise, waited until the slave emerged, and killed him with an iron mallet concealed in his sleeve; the other could not be found.

sentences.zh: 檝不欲見繼母，葬父畢，號慟曰：「父仇尚在，何以為人！

translations.literal: Ji would not see his stepmother; when his father's burial was finished he wailed, saying, "My father's enemy is still alive—how can I remain among men!
translations.idiomatic: Ji refused to see his stepmother. After burying his father he cried out, "My father's murderer still lives—how can I face the world!

sentences.zh: 」乃裂衣冠，屏妻子，出宿郊墟間，蓬首垢面，饑寒風雨，不知就避。

translations.literal: " He then tore his robes and cap, put wife and children aside, and slept out in ruined suburbs, hair disheveled and face filthy, enduring hunger, cold, wind, and rain without knowing where to seek shelter.
translations.idiomatic: " He tore his clothes, left his wife and children, and slept in ruined suburbs—unkempt, filthy, exposed to hunger, cold, wind, and rain with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 親戚故人率目之為狂，檝終不自明也。

translations.literal: Kin and old friends all regarded him as mad; Ji to the end never explained himself.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and friends all thought him mad; Ji never offered any explanation.

sentences.zh: 子燾卒，不哭。

translations.literal: When his son Tao died, he did not weep.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Tao died, he did not mourn.

sentences.zh: 或詰之，則垂涕曰：「我不能為子，敢為父乎！

translations.literal: When questioned, he shed tears and said, "I could not be a son—how dare I act as a father!
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, he wept and said, "I failed my father—how dare I grieve as a father should?

sentences.zh: 」繼母卒，乃歸。

translations.literal: " When his stepmother died, he then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: " Only when his stepmother died did he return home.

sentences.zh: 蓋自廢自罰者三十五年，又十五年而卒。

translations.literal: In all he had punished himself for thirty-five years, and fifteen years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He had punished himself in this way for thirty-five years, and died fifteen years after his return.

sentences.zh: 楊成章，道州人。

translations.literal: Yang Chengzang was a man of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chengzang was a native of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 父泰，為浙江長亭巡檢。

translations.literal: His father Tai was patrol inspector of Changting in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tai served as patrol inspector of Changting in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 妻何氏無出，納丁氏女為妾，生成章。

translations.literal: His wife the Lady He bore no children; he took the Ding family's daughter as concubine, who bore Chengzang.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady He was childless; he took a Ding girl as concubine, and she bore Chengzang.

sentences.zh: 甫四歲，泰卒。

translations.literal: When he was just four, Tai died.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzang was only four when Tai died.

sentences.zh: 何將扶櫬歸，丁氏父予之子，而奪其母。

translations.literal: He was about to shoulder the coffin home when the Ding girl's father gave her in marriage to another and took away her mother.
translations.idiomatic: As He was preparing to carry the coffin home, the Ding girl's father married her off elsewhere and took her mother away.

sentences.zh: 母乃剪銀錢與何別，約各藏其半，俟成章長授之。

translations.literal: The mother then cut a silver coin in two as a parting token with He, agreeing each should keep half to give Chengzang when he grew up.
translations.idiomatic: Before parting, the mother split a silver coin with He, each keeping half to give Chengzang when he came of age.

sentences.zh: 越六年，何臨歿，授成章半錢，告之故。

translations.literal: Six years later, as He lay dying, she gave Chengzang the half coin and told him the story.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later, on her deathbed, He gave Chengzang her half of the coin and told him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 成章嗚咽受命。

translations.literal: Chengzang sobbed and accepted the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzang wept and accepted the charge.

sentences.zh: 既冠，娶婦月余，即執半錢之浙中尋母。

translations.literal: When he came of age, a month after marrying he took the half coin and went to Zhejiang to seek his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After coming of age he married; a month later he set out for Zhejiang with the half coin to find his mother.

sentences.zh: 母先已適東陽郭氏，生子曰瑉，而成章不知也。

translations.literal: His mother had already remarried into the Guo family of Dongyang and borne a son named Min, of which Chengzang knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had already remarried into the Guo family of Dongyang and borne a son named Min, though Chengzang knew nothing of this.

sentences.zh: 遍訪之，無所遇而還。

translations.literal: He searched everywhere but found nothing and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He searched far and wide but found no trace and returned home.

sentences.zh: 弘治十一年，東陽典史李紹裔以事宿瑉家。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Hongzhi, Dongyang clerk Li Shaoyi lodged at Min's home on business.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Hongzhi, Li Shaoyi, clerk of Dongyang, stayed at Min's home on official business.

sentences.zh: 瑉母知為道州人，遣瑉問成章存否，知成章已為諸生，乃令瑉執半錢覓其兄。

translations.literal: Min's mother, learning he was from Daozhou, sent Min to ask whether Chengzang still lived; learning Chengzang was already a licentiate, she had Min take the half coin to seek his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Min's mother, hearing he was from Daozhou, sent Min to ask after Chengzang; learning Chengzang was now a licentiate, she told Min to take the half coin and find his brother.

sentences.zh: 會有會稽人官訓導者，嘗設教東陽，為瑉師，與成章述瑉母憶子狀。

translations.literal: It happened that a man from Kuaiji serving as educational instructor had once taught in Dongyang and was Min's teacher; he told Chengzang how Min's mother yearned for her son.
translations.idiomatic: A Kuaiji man serving as educational instructor in Dongyang, who had been Min's teacher, told Chengzang how Min's mother longed for her lost son.

sentences.zh: 成章亦往尋母，遇瑉於江西舟次。

translations.literal: Chengzang also went to seek his mother and met Min aboard a boat in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzang set out again to find his mother and met Min on a boat in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 兄弟悲且喜，各出半錢合之，益信，遂俱至東陽，母子始相聚。

translations.literal: The brothers grieved and rejoiced; each produced his half coin and joined them, trusting all the more, and went together to Dongyang, where mother and sons were reunited at last.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers wept and rejoiced, fitted their half coins together, and went on to Dongyang, where mother and sons were reunited.

sentences.zh: 自是成章三往迎母不遂，棄月廩，赴東陽侍養。

translations.literal: From then on Chengzang thrice went to bring his mother but failed; he gave up his monthly stipend and went to Dongyang to serve and support her.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzang tried three times to bring his mother home without success; he gave up his stipend and went to Dongyang to care for her.

sentences.zh: 及母卒，廬墓三載始返。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he dwelt by the tomb for three years before returning.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he kept vigil at her grave for three years before returning home.

sentences.zh: 至嘉靖十年，成章以歲貢入都，瑉亦以事至，乃述成章尋親事，上之吏部，請進一官。

translations.literal: By the tenth year of Jiajing, Chengzang entered the capital as a tribute student and Min also arrived on business; he recounted Chengzang's search for kin and submitted it to the Ministry of Personnel, requesting one step of promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jiajing, Chengzang came to the capital as a tribute student and Min arrived on business; Min reported Chengzang's quest for his mother to the Ministry of Personnel and asked that he be promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 部臣言：「成章孝行，兩地已勘實，登之朝覲憲綱，瑉言非謬。

translations.literal: The ministry officials said, "Chengzang's filial conduct has been verified in both places and entered in the regulations for court audience; Min's account is not false.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry replied, "Chengzang's filial conduct has been verified in both places and recorded in the regulations for court audience; Min's account is accurate.

sentences.zh: 昔朱壽昌棄官尋母，宋神宗詔令就官。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhu Shouchang abandoned office to seek his mother, and Emperor Shenzong of Song ordered him to resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the Song, Zhu Shouchang left office to find his mother, and Emperor Shenzong ordered him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 今所司知而不能薦，臣等又拘例而不請旌，真有愧於古誼。

translations.literal: Now the local offices knew but could not recommend, and we were bound by precedent and did not request commendation—truly we have failed the ancient meaning of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Today the local authorities knew but failed to recommend him, and we were bound by precedent and did not request commendation—we have fallen short of ancient righteousness.

sentences.zh: 請量授成章國子學錄，賜瑉花紅羊酒。

translations.literal: We request that Chengzang be appointed recorder of the Imperial Academy as appropriate, and that Min be granted floral honors, red cloth, a sheep, and wine.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Chengzang be appointed recorder of the Imperial Academy and that Min receive floral honors, red cloth, a sheep, and wine.

translations.literal: " The decree said, "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor decreed, "Let it be so."

sentences.zh: 謝用，字希中，祁門人。

translations.literal: Xie Yong, style name Xizhong, was a man of Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yong, styled Xizhong, was a native of Qimen.

sentences.zh: 父永貞。

translations.literal: His father was Yongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Yongzhen.

sentences.zh: 生母馬氏方妊，永貞客外，嫡母汪氏妒而嫁之，遂生用。

translations.literal: His birth mother the Lady Ma was pregnant when Yongzhen was away; the legal mother Lady Wang, jealous, married her off, and thus Yong was born.
translations.idiomatic: His birth mother Lady Ma was pregnant when Yongzhen was away on business; the legal wife Lady Wang, jealous, married Ma off elsewhere, and Yong was born.

sentences.zh: 永貞還，大恨，抱用歸，寄乳鄰媼。

translations.literal: When Yongzhen returned he was greatly angered, took Yong home, and entrusted him to a neighbor wet-nurse.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongzhen returned he was furious, took the infant home, and placed him with a neighbor to nurse.

sentences.zh: 汪氏收而自鞠之，逾年亦生子，均愛無厚薄。

translations.literal: Lady Wang took him back and reared him herself; a year later she too bore a son, and loved both without partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang took him back and raised him herself; the next year she bore a son of her own and loved both boys equally.

sentences.zh: 用既冠，始知所生。

translations.literal: When Yong came of age he first learned who had borne him.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Yong came of age did he learn who his birth mother was.

sentences.zh: 密訪之，則又改適，不知其所矣。

translations.literal: He secretly sought her, but she had remarried again and her whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: He searched for her in secret, but she had married again and could not be found.

sentences.zh: 用遍覓幾一載。

translations.literal: Yong searched everywhere for nearly a year.
translations.idiomatic: Yong searched for nearly a year.

sentences.zh: 一夕宿休寧農家，有寡嫗出問曰：「若為誰？

translations.literal: One night he lodged at a farmer's house in Xiuning; a widowed old woman came out and asked, "Who are you?
translations.idiomatic: One night he stayed at a farmhouse in Xiuning; a widow came out and asked, "Who are you?

sentences.zh: 」用告以姓名，及尋母之故。

translations.literal: " Yong told his name and the reason he sought his mother.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong gave his name and explained that he was searching for his mother.

sentences.zh: 曰：「若母為誰？

translations.literal: She said, "Who is your mother?
translations.idiomatic: She asked, "Who is your mother?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「馬氏。

translations.literal: " He said, "The Lady Ma.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "Lady Ma.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「若非永貞之子乎？

translations.literal: " She said, "Are you not Yongzhen's son?
translations.idiomatic: " She said, "Are you not Yongzhen's son?

translations.literal: " He said, "Yes.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "I am.

sentences.zh: 」媼遂抱用曰：「我即汝母也。

translations.literal: " The old woman then embraced Yong and said, "I am your mother.
translations.idiomatic: " The old woman embraced him and said, "I am your mother.

sentences.zh: 」於是母子相持而哭，時弘治十五年四月也。

translations.literal: " Then mother and son clung to each other and wept—it was the fourth month of the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: " Mother and son held each other and wept. It was the fourth month of the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 用歸告父，並其同母弟迎歸，居別室。

translations.literal: Yong returned and told his father, and together with his younger brother of the same mother brought her home to live in a separate chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Yong went home and told his father; together with his younger brother by the same mother they brought her home to a separate dwelling.

sentences.zh: 孝養二母，曲盡其誠。

translations.literal: He filially supported both mothers with utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for both mothers with devoted filial piety.

sentences.zh: 後汪感悔，令迎馬同居，訖無間言。

translations.literal: Later Wang, moved to repentance, had Ma welcomed to live together, and to the end there was no discord.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lady Wang repented and had Ma brought to live in the same house; they never quarreled again.

sentences.zh: 永貞卒，用居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: When Yongzhen died, Yong's mourning conduct was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongzhen died, Yong's mourning was renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 鄰人失火，延數十家，將至用舍，風反火息。

translations.literal: A neighbor's fire spread to dozens of houses and was about to reach Yong's dwelling when the wind shifted and the fire died.
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor's fire spread to dozens of houses and threatened Yong's home, the wind shifted and the flames died out.

sentences.zh: 用時為諸生，督學御史廉其孝，列之德行優等，月廩之。

translations.literal: Yong was then a licentiate; the education intendant, admiring his filial piety, ranked him in the top grade of moral conduct and granted him a monthly stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was then a licentiate; the education intendant, recognizing his filial piety, ranked him in the top grade of moral conduct and granted him a monthly stipend.

sentences.zh: 何競，字邦植，蕭山人。

translations.literal: He Jing, style name Bangzhi, was a man of Xiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: He Jing, styled Bangzhi, was a native of Xiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 父舜賓，為御史，謫戍廣西慶遠衛，遇赦還。

translations.literal: His father Shunbin was a censor, banished to garrison duty at Qingyuan Guard in Guangxi, and returned on amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shunbin had served as a censor, was banished to Qingyuan Guard in Guangxi, and returned on amnesty.

sentences.zh: 好持吏短長。

translations.literal: He liked to seize on officials' faults.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of exposing officials' misdeeds.

sentences.zh: 有鄒魯者，當塗人。

translations.literal: There was a Zou Lu, a man of Dangtu.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Zou Lu of Dangtu.

sentences.zh: 亦以御史謫官，稍遷蕭山知縣，貪暴狡悍。

translations.literal: He too had been demoted from the censorate and was gradually promoted to magistrate of Xiaoshan, greedy, violent, and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: He too had been demoted from the censorate and later became magistrate of Xiaoshan—a greedy, violent, and ruthless man.

sentences.zh: 舜賓求魯陰事訐之，兩人互相猜。

translations.literal: Shunbin sought Lu's secret faults to impeach him, and the two mutually suspected each other.
translations.idiomatic: Shunbin sought out Lu's secret misdeeds to impeach him, and the two became bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 縣中湘湖為富人私據，舜賓發其事於官，奏核之。

translations.literal: In the county, Xiang Lake was privately seized by the rich; Shunbin exposed the matter to the authorities and memorialized for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families had illegally seized Xiang Lake in the county; Shunbin reported this to the authorities and memorialized for an investigation.

sentences.zh: 富人因奏舜賓以戍卒潛逃，擅自冠帶。

translations.literal: The rich therefore memorialized that Shunbin had allowed garrison soldiers to flee secretly and had worn cap and belt without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy families then memorialized that Shunbin had allowed garrison soldiers to desert and had worn official dress without authorization.

sentences.zh: 章並下所司核治。

translations.literal: Both memorials were sent down to the relevant offices for investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Both memorials were sent to the relevant offices for investigation.

sentences.zh: 魯隱其文牒，詭言舜賓遇赦無驗，宜行原衛查核。

translations.literal: Lu concealed the documents and falsely said Shunbin's amnesty could not be verified and that he should be sent back to his original guard for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Lu concealed the documents and falsely claimed Shunbin's amnesty could not be verified and that he should be sent back to his original guard.

sentences.zh: 上官不可，駁之。

translations.literal: The superior would not agree and rejected this.
translations.idiomatic: His superiors refused and rejected the proposal.

sentences.zh: 會舜賓門人訓導童顯章為魯所陷論死，下府覆驗，道經舜賓家，入與謀。

translations.literal: It happened that Shunbin's student, educational instructor Tong Xianzhang, was framed by Lu and sentenced to death; when sent down to the prefecture for review he passed Shunbin's home and entered to consult with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shunbin's student Tong Xianzhang, an educational instructor, was framed by Lu and condemned to death; on the way to the prefecture for review he stopped at Shunbin's home to consult with him.

sentences.zh: 魯聞之，大詬曰：「舜賓乃敢竄重囚。

translations.literal: Lu heard of it and cursed loudly, saying, "Shunbin dares harbor a serious criminal!
translations.idiomatic: When Lu learned of this he raged, "Shunbin dares harbor a condemned prisoner!

sentences.zh: 」發卒圍其門，輒捕舜賓，徑解慶遠。

translations.literal: " He sent soldiers to surround the gate, seized Shunbin at once, and escorted him straight to Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent soldiers to surround the house, seized Shunbin, and sent him straight back to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 又令爪牙吏屏其衣服。

translations.literal: He also ordered his henchmen to strip away his clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered his henchmen to strip Shunbin of his clothes.

sentences.zh: 至余幹，宿昌國寺，夜以濕衣閉其口，壓殺之。

translations.literal: At Yugan he lodged at Changguo Temple; at night they stuffed his mouth with wet cloth and smothered him to death.
translations.idiomatic: At Yugan he was lodged at Changguo Temple; that night they stuffed his mouth with wet cloth and smothered him.

sentences.zh: 魯復捕舜賓妻子。

translations.literal: Lu again seized Shunbin's wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Lu then arrested Shunbin's wife and children.

sentences.zh: 競與母逃常熟，匿父友王鼎家。

translations.literal: Jing fled with his mother to Changshu and hid in the home of his father's friend Wang Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Jing fled with his mother to Changshu and hid in the home of his father's friend Wang Ding.

sentences.zh: —已而魯遷山西僉事，將行。

translations.literal: —Later Lu was transferred to be surveillance commissioner of Shanxi and was about to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lu was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Shanxi and was about to leave.

sentences.zh: 競乃潛歸與族人謀，召親黨數十人飲之酒，為舜賓稱冤。

translations.literal: Jing secretly returned and consulted with his clansmen, summoned several dozen kin, feasted them with wine, and spoke of Shunbin's wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing slipped home and consulted with his clansmen, gathered several dozen relatives, feasted them, and spoke of his father's injustice.

sentences.zh: 中坐，競出叩首哭以請，皆踴躍願效命。

translations.literal: Mid-feast, Jing came forward, kowtowed and wept in petition, and all leapt up willing to give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Midway through the feast Jing kowtowed and wept, begging their help, and all leapt up eager to serve.

sentences.zh: 乃各持器伏道旁，伺魯過，競袖鐵捶奮擊，騶從駭散。

translations.literal: Each then took weapons and lay in wait by the road; when Lu passed, Jing struck fiercely with an iron mallet hidden in his sleeve, and the escort scattered in terror.
translations.idiomatic: They armed themselves and lay in wait by the road; when Lu passed, Jing struck with an iron mallet hidden in his sleeve, and Lu's escort fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 仆其輿，裸之，杖齊下，霍兩目，須發盡拔。

translations.literal: They overturned his carriage, stripped him naked, and beat him together; both eyes were put out and beard and hair torn out entirely.
translations.idiomatic: They overturned his carriage, stripped him naked, and beat him until both eyes were destroyed and his beard and hair torn out.

sentences.zh: 競拔佩刀砍其左股，必欲殺之，為眾所止。

translations.literal: Jing drew his belt knife and hacked Lu's left thigh, determined to kill him, but was stopped by the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Jing drew his knife and slashed Lu's left thigh, intent on killing him, but the others restrained him.

sentences.zh: 乃與魯連鎖赴按察司，而預令族父澤走闕下訴冤。

translations.literal: They then chained Lu and Jing together and went to the surveillance commission, while beforehand Jing had ordered his clansman Ze to run to the capital to plead the wrong.
translations.idiomatic: They chained Lu and Jing together and went to the surveillance commission, while Jing had already sent his clansman Ze to the capital to petition for justice.

sentences.zh: 僉事蕭翀故黨魯，嚴刑訊競。

translations.literal: Commissioner Xiao Chong was formerly Lu's partisan and tortured Jing severely.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Xiao Chong, an old ally of Lu's, tortured Jing severely.

sentences.zh: 競大言曰：「必欲殺我，我非畏死者。

translations.literal: Jing declared loudly, "If you must kill me, I am not one who fears death.
translations.idiomatic: Jing cried out, "If you mean to kill me, I do not fear death.

sentences.zh: 顧人孰無父母，且我已訟於朝，非公輩所得擅殺。

translations.literal: Only consider—who lacks parents? Moreover I have already sued at court; you lot have no right to kill me on your own.
translations.idiomatic: But who among us has no parents? And I have already petitioned the throne—you have no right to kill me on your own authority.

sentences.zh: 」噬臂肉擲案上，含血噀翀面，一堂皆驚。

translations.literal: ] He bit flesh from his arm and threw it onto the table, held blood in his mouth and sprayed it on Chong's face—the whole hall was shocked.
translations.idiomatic: ] He bit flesh from his own arm and flung it on the table, then spat blood in Xiao Chong's face, shocking everyone present.

sentences.zh: 會競疏已上，遣刑部郎中李時、給事中李舉，會巡按御史鄧璋雜治。

translations.literal: When Jing's memorial had already been submitted, Li Shi of the Ministry of Punishments and Li Ju of the Secretariat were dispatched to join investigating censor Deng Zhang in a joint trial.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jing's petition reached the throne, the court sent Li Shi of the Ministry of Punishments and Li Ju of the Secretariat to conduct a joint investigation with touring censor Deng Zhang.

sentences.zh: 諸人持兩端，擬魯故屏人衣食至死，競部民毆本屬知縣篤疾，律俱絞，余所逮數百人，擬罪有差。

translations.literal: The officials sat on both sides; Lu was proposed to be sentenced for deliberately secluding a man and withholding food and clothing until death; Jing's clansmen beat the county magistrate of their district to grave illness—by law both strangulation; the several hundred others arrested received varying proposed sentences.
translations.idiomatic: The officials hedged their verdicts: Lu was to be sentenced for secretly imprisoning a man and starving him to death, while Jing's clansmen were held to have beaten their own county magistrate nearly to death—both capital offenses by law. The several hundred others arrested received differing sentences.

sentences.zh: 競母朱氏復撾登聞鼓訴冤，魯亦使人馳訴，乃命大理寺正曹廉會巡按御史陳銓覆治。

translations.literal: Jing's mother the Zhu clan again struck the drum of grievance to plead injustice; Lu also sent someone racing to appeal; thereupon Director of the Court of Judicial Review Cao Lian was ordered to join investigating censor Chen Quan in a retrial.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's mother, Lady Zhu, again beat the drum of grievance at the capital to protest the injustice, and Lu dispatched an urgent appeal as well. The court then ordered Cao Lian, director of the Court of Judicial Review, to retry the case jointly with touring censor Chen Quan.

sentences.zh: 廉曰：「爾等何毆縣官？

translations.literal: Cao said: "Why did you all beat the county official?
translations.idiomatic: Cao asked, "Why did you assault the county magistrate?

sentences.zh: 」競曰：「競知父仇，不知縣官，但恨未殺之耳。

translations.literal: ] Jing said: "Jing knew his father's enemy, not that he was a county official—he only regrets not having killed him.
translations.idiomatic: ] Jing replied, "I knew my father's enemy, not a county magistrate. I only regret that I did not kill him.

sentences.zh: 」廉以致死無據，遣縣令揭棺驗之。

translations.literal: ] As there was no evidence of death by beating, Cao sent the county magistrate to open the coffin and examine the body.
translations.idiomatic: ] Finding no proof that the beating had been fatal, Cao ordered the county magistrate to open the coffin and examine the corpse.

sentences.zh: 驗者報傷，而解役任寬慷慨首實，且出舜賓臨命所付血書。

translations.literal: The examiners reported injuries; and released laborer Ren Kuan boldly confessed first, and moreover produced the blood-letter Shunbin had entrusted at his dying moment.
translations.idiomatic: The examiners reported injuries, and the released corvée laborer Ren Kuan stepped forward to confess, producing the blood-stained letter Shunbin had entrusted to him at the point of death.

sentences.zh: 於是眾皆辭伏，改擬魯斬，競徒三年。

translations.literal: Thereupon all confessed; the proposal was changed to decapitation for Lu and three years' penal servitude for Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all confessed, and the sentences were revised to decapitation for Lu and three years of penal servitude for Jing.

sentences.zh: 法司議競遣戍，且曰：「魯已成篤疾，競為父報仇，律意有在，均俟上裁。

translations.literal: The judicial offices proposed exile for Jing, and said: "Lu is already gravely ill; Jing avenged his father—the spirit of the law has room for this; both await the sovereign's decision.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices recommended banishing Jing instead, arguing: "Lu is already gravely ill, and Jing acted to avenge his father—the law allows for such circumstances. Both cases should await the emperor's judgment.

sentences.zh: 」帝從其議，戍競福寧衛，時弘治十四年二月也。

translations.literal: ] The emperor accepted their proposal, exiled Jing to Funing Guard—it was the second month of the fourteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: ] The emperor accepted their recommendation and banished Jing to Funing Guard. This was in the second month of the fourteenth year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 後武宗登極肆赦，魯免死，競赦歸，又九年卒。

translations.literal: Later when the Wuzong emperor ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty, Lu was spared death and Jing was pardoned and returned; nine years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty, Lu was spared execution and Jing was pardoned and sent home. Nine years after that, Jing died.

sentences.zh: 競自父歿至死，凡十六年，服衰終其身。

translations.literal: From his father's death until his own, sixteen years in all; he wore mourning garb to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: From his father's death until his own, sixteen years passed, and he wore mourning dress for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 王原，文安人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuan, a native of Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan was a native of Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 正德中，父珣以家貧役重逃去。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign, his father Xun fled because the family was poor and corvée burdens heavy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign, his father Xun fled home because the family was poor and corvée duties were crushing.

sentences.zh: 原稍長，問父所在。

translations.literal: When Yuan had grown somewhat, he asked where his father was.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan had grown up a little, he asked where his father had gone.

sentences.zh: 母告以故，原大悲慟。

translations.literal: His mother told him the circumstances, and Yuan grieved bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: His mother told him what had happened, and Yuan was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 乃設肆於邑治之衢，治酒食舍諸行旅。

translations.literal: He then set up a shop at the crossroads near the county seat, preparing wine and food to lodge travelers.
translations.idiomatic: He then opened a shop at the crossroads by the county seat, preparing food and wine to lodge passing travelers.

sentences.zh: 遇遠方客至，則告以父姓名、年貌，冀得父蹤跡。

translations.literal: When distant guests arrived, he would tell them his father's name, age, and appearance, hoping to learn his father's whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever travelers from afar stopped in, he would describe his father's name, age, and appearance, hoping to pick up some trace of him.

sentences.zh: 久之無所得。

translations.literal: After a long time he gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he learned nothing.

sentences.zh: 既娶婦月余，跪告母曰：「兒將尋父。

translations.literal: Having married a wife for a little over a month, he knelt and told his mother: "Your son will go seek Father.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month after he married, he knelt before his mother and said, "I am going to search for Father.

sentences.zh: 」母泣曰：「汝父去二十余載，存亡不可知。

translations.literal: ] His mother wept and said: "Your father has been gone more than twenty years; whether he lives or not cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: ] His mother wept and said, "Your father has been gone more than twenty years. We cannot even know whether he is alive.

sentences.zh: 且若父氓耳，流落何所，誰知名者？

translations.literal: Moreover your father was but a common fellow—where would he drift, and who would know his name?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, he was only an ordinary man—who knows where he may have wandered, or who would recognize his name?

sentences.zh: 無為父子相繼作羈鬼，使我無依。

translations.literal: Do not let father and son in succession become wandering ghosts and leave me with none to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let father and son become wandering ghosts in turn and leave me with no one to depend on.

sentences.zh: 」原痛哭曰：「幸有婦陪母，母無以兒為念，兒不得父不歸也。

translations.literal: ] Yuan wept bitterly and said: "Fortunately I have a wife to keep you company—Mother, do not think of your son; I shall not return without finding Father.
translations.idiomatic: ] Yuan wept and said, "Fortunately my wife can keep you company. Do not worry about me, Mother—I will not come home without finding Father.

sentences.zh: 」號泣辭母去，遍歷山東南北，去來者數年。

translations.literal: ] Wailing he bade his mother farewell and went, traveling throughout north and south Shandong, coming and going for several years.
translations.idiomatic: ] Weeping, he took leave of his mother and set out, traveling back and forth across Shandong for several years.

sentences.zh: 一日，渡海至田橫島，假寐神祠中，夢至一寺，當午，炊莎和肉羹食之。

translations.literal: One day he crossed the sea to Tianheng Island, dozed in a spirit shrine, and dreamed he reached a temple; at noon he cooked sedge with meat broth and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: One day he crossed the sea to Tianheng Island and dozed in a spirit shrine. In a dream he came to a temple where, at noon, he cooked sedge root with meat into a broth and ate it.

sentences.zh: 一老父至，驚覺。

translations.literal: An old man came, and he woke with a start.
translations.idiomatic: An old man arrived, and he woke with a start.

sentences.zh: 原告之夢，請占之。

translations.literal: Yuan told him the dream and asked him to interpret it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan told him the dream and asked him to interpret it.

sentences.zh: 老父曰：「若何為者？

translations.literal: The old man said: "What is your business?
translations.idiomatic: The old man asked, "What brings you here?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「尋父。

translations.literal: ] He said: "Seeking my father.
translations.idiomatic: ] He said, "I am searching for my father.

sentences.zh: 」老父曰：「午者，正南位也。

translations.literal: ] The old man said: "Noon is the due-south position.
translations.idiomatic: ] The old man said, "Noon stands for due south.

sentences.zh: 莎根附子，肉和之，附子膾也。

translations.literal: Sedge root is aconite; meat mixed with it is aconite mince.
translations.idiomatic: Sedge root is aconite, and meat mixed with it makes aconite hash—a homophone for 'father and son meet.'

sentences.zh: 求諸南方，父子其會乎？

translations.literal: Seek in the south—perhaps father and son will meet?
translations.idiomatic: Search toward the south. Perhaps father and son will be reunited?

sentences.zh: 」原喜，謝去，而南踰洺、漳，至輝縣帶山，有寺曰夢覺，原心動。

translations.literal: ] Yuan was pleased, thanked him and left, and went south beyond Handan and Zhangzhou to Dai Mountain in Huixian, where there was a temple called Mengjue; Yuan's heart stirred.
translations.idiomatic: ] Yuan was delighted, thanked him, and set off south beyond Handan and Zhangzhou to Dai Mountain in Huixian, where he found a temple called Awakening from a Dream. His heart stirred.

sentences.zh: 天雨雪，寒甚，臥寺門外。

translations.literal: Snow fell from heaven; the cold was extreme, and he lay outside the temple gate.
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell from the sky and the cold was fierce, so he lay down outside the temple gate.

sentences.zh: 及曙，一僧啟門出，駭曰：「汝何人？

translations.literal: At dawn a monk opened the door and came out, startled, and said: "Who are you?
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak a monk opened the door and, startled, asked, "Who are you?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「文安人，尋父而來。

translations.literal: ] He said: "A man of Wen'an, come seeking my father.
translations.idiomatic: ] He answered, "I am from Wen'an. I have come searching for my father.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「識之乎？

translations.literal: ] He said: "Do you know him?
translations.idiomatic: ] The monk asked, "Do you know him?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不識也。

translations.literal: ] He said: "I do not.
translations.idiomatic: ] He said, "I do not.

sentences.zh: 」引入禪堂，憐而予之粥。

translations.literal: ] He was led into the meditation hall; pitying him, the monk gave him porridge.
translations.idiomatic: ] The monk led him into the meditation hall, took pity on him, and gave him congee.

sentences.zh: 珣方執爨竈下，僧素知為文安人，謂之曰：「若同里有少年來尋父者，若倘識其人。

translations.literal: Xun was just tending the kitchen fire beneath the stove; the monk, knowing he was from Wen'an, said to him: "A young man from your home district has come seeking his father—perhaps you know the man.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was tending the kitchen fire beneath the stove. The monk, knowing he was from Wen'an, said to him, "A young man from your home district has come looking for his father. Perhaps you know him.

sentences.zh: 」珣出見原，皆不相識，問其父姓名，則王珣也。

translations.literal: ] Xun came out to see Yuan; neither recognized the other; when asked his father's name, it was Wang Xun.
translations.idiomatic: ] Xun came out to see Yuan. Neither recognized the other until Yuan was asked his father's name—it was Wang Xun.

sentences.zh: 珣亦呼原乳名。

translations.literal: Xun also called Yuan by his childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Xun then called Yuan by his childhood name.

sentences.zh: 相抱持慟哭，寺僧莫不感動。

translations.literal: They embraced and wept bitterly; not one monk in the temple was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: They embraced and wept, and every monk in the temple was moved.

sentences.zh: 珣曰：「歸告汝母，我無顏復歸故鄉矣。

translations.literal: Xun said: "Go tell your mother—I have no face to return to my old home.
translations.idiomatic: Xun said, "Go tell your mother that I am too ashamed to return to our old home.

sentences.zh: 」原曰：「父不歸，兒有死耳。

translations.literal: ] Yuan said: "If Father does not return, your son has only death.
translations.idiomatic: ] Yuan said, "If you do not come home, Father, your son would rather die.

sentences.zh: 」牽衣哭不止。

translations.literal: ] Pulling his clothes he wept without cease.
translations.idiomatic: ] He clutched his father's clothes and wept without stopping.

sentences.zh: 寺僧力勸之，父子相持歸，夫妻子母復聚。

translations.literal: The temple monks urged them strongly; father and son supported each other home, and husband, wife, son, and mother were reunited.
translations.idiomatic: The monks urged them on, and father and son made their way home together. Husband, wife, son, and mother were reunited at last.

sentences.zh: 後原子孫多仕宦者。

translations.literal: Later many of Yuan's descendants entered official service.
translations.idiomatic: Later many of Yuan's descendants rose to office.

sentences.zh: 黃璽，字廷璽，余姚人。

translations.literal: Huang Xi, courtesy name Tingxi, a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xi, styled Tingxi, was a native of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 兄伯震，商十年不歸。

translations.literal: His elder brother Bozhen traded and did not return for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Bozhen went into trade and did not return for ten years.

sentences.zh: 璽出求之，經行萬里，不得蹤跡。

translations.literal: Xi went out to seek him, traveled ten thousand li, and found no trace.
translations.idiomatic: Xi set out to find him, traveled ten thousand li, and discovered no trace.

sentences.zh: 最後至衡州，禱南嶽廟，夢神人授以「纏綿盜賊際，狼狽江漢行」二句。

translations.literal: At last he reached Hengzhou, prayed at the Southern Sacred Peak temple, and dreamed a spirit gave him two lines: "Entangled amid bandits, in distress traveling the Jiang and Han."
translations.idiomatic: At last he reached Hengzhou and prayed at the temple of the Southern Sacred Peak. In a dream a spirit gave him two lines: "Entangled amid bandits, struggling along the Jiang and Han."

sentences.zh: 一書生告之曰：「此杜甫《舂陵行》詩也，舂陵今道州，曷往尋之。

translations.literal: A scholar told him: "This is Du Fu's poem 'Chunling Line'—Chunling is today's Daozhou; why not go seek there?
translations.idiomatic: A scholar told him, "Those lines come from Du Fu's 'Song of Chunling.' Chunling is present-day Daozhou—why not search there?

sentences.zh: 」璽從其言，既至，無所遇。

translations.literal: ] Xi followed his words; once arrived, he met with nothing.
translations.idiomatic: ] Xi took his advice, but once he arrived he found nothing.

sentences.zh: 一日入廁，置傘道旁。

translations.literal: One day he entered a privy and left his umbrella by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: One day he entered a privy and left his umbrella by the road.

sentences.zh: 伯震適過之曰：此吾鄉之傘也。

translations.literal: Bozhen happened to pass and said: "This is an umbrella from our home district."
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen happened to pass by and said, "This umbrella is from our home district."

sentences.zh: 」循其柄而觀，見有「余姚黃廷璽記」六字。

translations.literal: ] Following the handle and looking, he saw six characters: "Recorded by Huang Tingxi of Yuyao."
translations.idiomatic: ] He followed the handle with his eyes and saw six characters inscribed there: "Recorded by Huang Tingxi of Yuyao."

sentences.zh: 方疑駭，璽出問訊，則其兄也，遂奉以歸。

translations.literal: Just as he doubted in alarm, Xi came out to greet him—it was his elder brother; he then escorted him home.
translations.idiomatic: Still puzzled and startled, Xi came out to greet him—it was his elder brother—and he escorted him home.

sentences.zh: 歸鉞，字汝威，嘉定縣人。

translations.literal: Gui Yue, courtesy name Ruwei, a native of Jiading county.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Yue, styled Ruwei, was a native of Jiading county.

sentences.zh: 早喪母。

translations.literal: He lost his mother early.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother at an early age.

sentences.zh: 父娶繼妻，有子，鉞遂失愛。

translations.literal: His father took a stepmother and had a son; Yue then lost favor.
translations.idiomatic: His father remarried and had another son, and Yue fell out of favor.

sentences.zh: 父偶撻鉞，繼母輒索大杖與之，曰：「毋傷乃翁力也。

translations.literal: When his father occasionally whipped Yue, the stepmother would demand a large staff and give it to him, saying: "Do not waste your husband's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his father happened to beat Yue, the stepmother would fetch a heavier rod and hand it to him, saying, "Don't tire yourself out, husband.

sentences.zh: 」家貧，食不足，每炊將熟，即諓諓數鉞過，父怒而逐之，其母子得飽食。

translations.literal: ] The family was poor and food insufficient; whenever the rice was nearly cooked she would chatter criticisms of Yue as he passed; his father would fly into rage and drive him off, and the stepmother and her son ate their fill.
translations.idiomatic: ] The family was poor and there was never enough food. Whenever the meal was nearly ready, she would nag about Yue as he passed by; his father would fly into a rage and drive him out, and the stepmother and her son ate their fill.

sentences.zh: 鉞饑困，匍匐道中。

translations.literal: Yue, hungry and exhausted, crawled on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Hungry and exhausted, Yue crawled along the road.

sentences.zh: 比歸，父母相與言曰：「有子不居家，在外作賊耳。

translations.literal: When he returned, father and stepmother said to each other: "A son who does not stay home must be out being a thief.
translations.idiomatic: When he came home, his father and stepmother said to each other, "A son who won't stay at home must be out stealing.

sentences.zh: 」輒復杖之，屢瀕於死。

translations.literal: ] They would beat him again, repeatedly bringing him near death.
translations.idiomatic: ] They would beat him again, repeatedly bringing him to the brink of death.

sentences.zh: 及父卒，母益擯不納，因販鹽市中，時私其弟，問母飲食，致甘鮮焉。

translations.literal: After his father died, his mother pushed him away further and would not take him in; he therefore sold salt in the market, secretly helping his younger brother, asking after his mother's food and drink, and sending delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: After his father died, his stepmother rejected him still more firmly, so he took to selling salt in the market. From time to time he secretly gave money to his younger brother, inquired after his mother's meals, and sent her fine foods.

sentences.zh: 正德三年，大饑，母不能自活。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde there was a great famine; his mother could not support herself.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhengde reign there was a severe famine, and his stepmother could no longer support herself.

sentences.zh: 鉞涕泣奉迎，母內自慚不欲往，然以無所資，迄從之。

translations.literal: Yue wept and went to welcome her; inwardly ashamed she did not wish to go, but having no means, in the end she followed.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, Yue went to bring her home. Ashamed at heart, she did not wish to go, but having no other means of support, she went with him in the end.

sentences.zh: 鉞得食，先母弟，而己有饑色。

translations.literal: When Yue got food he gave first to his mother and brother, while he himself looked hungry.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yue obtained food, he gave first to his stepmother and brother, while he himself went hungry.

sentences.zh: 弟尋卒，鉞養母終其身，嘉靖中卒。

translations.literal: His younger brother soon died; Yue supported his mother to the end of her life and died in the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother soon died. Yue supported his stepmother for the rest of her life and passed away during the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 族子繡，亦販鹽，與二弟紋、緯友愛。

translations.literal: Clansman Xiu also sold salt, and was affectionate with his two younger brothers Wen and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Xiu also sold salt and was deeply devoted to his two younger brothers, Wen and Wei.

sentences.zh: 緯數犯法，繡輒罄貲護之，終無慍色。

translations.literal: Wei repeatedly broke the law; Xiu would exhaust his wealth to shield him, and to the end showed no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Wei repeatedly ran afoul of the law, and each time Xiu spent everything he had to protect him, yet never showed anger.

sentences.zh: 繡妻朱，制衣必三襲，曰：「二叔無室，豈可使郎君獨暖耶？

translations.literal: Xiu's wife Zhu, when making clothes always made three sets, saying: "The two uncles have no wives—how can the young masters alone be warm?
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's wife, Lady Zhu, always made three sets of clothes and said, "The two uncles have no wives of their own—how can our sons alone stay warm?

sentences.zh: 」裏人稱為歸氏二孝子。

translations.literal: ] Neighbors called them the two filial sons of the Gui clan.
translations.idiomatic: ] People in the neighborhood called them the two filial sons of the Gui clan.

sentences.zh: 何麟，沁水人，為布政司吏。

translations.literal: He Lin, a native of Qinshui, served as a clerk in the provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: He Lin, a native of Qinshui, was a clerk in the provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 武宗微行，由大同抵太原，城門閉，不得入。

translations.literal: The Wuzong emperor traveled incognito; from Datong he reached Taiyuan, but the city gates were closed and he could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong traveled in disguise. Coming from Datong to Taiyuan, he found the city gates shut and could not enter.

sentences.zh: 怒而還京，遣中官逮守臣不啟門者，巡撫以下皆大懼。

translations.literal: Enraged he returned to the capital and sent eunuchs to arrest the officials who had not opened the gates; from the governor on down all were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, he returned to the capital and sent eunuchs to arrest the officials who had refused to open the gates. From the provincial governor on down, all were terrified.

sentences.zh: 麟曰：「朝廷未知主名。

translations.literal: Lin said: "The court does not yet know the sovereign's identity.
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "The court does not yet know who the traveler really was.

sentences.zh: 請厚賄中官，麟與俱往。

translations.literal: Please bribe the eunuchs heavily; Lin will go with them.
translations.idiomatic: Bribe the eunuchs generously, and I will go with them.

sentences.zh: 即聖怒不測，麟一身獨當之。

translations.literal: Even if imperial wrath is unpredictable, Lin alone will bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the emperor's anger proves unpredictable, I alone will bear the consequences.

sentences.zh: 」及抵京，上疏曰：「陛下巡幸晉陽，司城門者實臣麟一人，他官無預也。

translations.literal: ] When they reached the capital he submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty toured Jinyang; the one who managed the city gate was in truth your servant Lin alone—no other official was involved.
translations.idiomatic: ] When they reached the capital he submitted a memorial: "When Your Majesty visited Jinyang, I, Lin, alone was responsible for the city gate. No other official was involved.

sentences.zh: 臣不能啟門迎駕，罪當萬死。

translations.literal: Your servant failed to open the gate to welcome the imperial carriage—his crime deserves ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant failed to open the gate to welcome the imperial carriage—a crime deserving death ten thousand times over.

sentences.zh: 但陛下輕宗廟社稷而事巡遊，且易服微行，無清道警蹕之詔，白龍魚服，臣下何由辨焉。

translations.literal: But Your Majesty has slighted the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain for touring, and moreover changed dress to travel incognito, with no decree for clearing the road and imperial escort—the white dragon in fish garb—how are officials below to distinguish?
translations.idiomatic: But Your Majesty set the ancestral temple and the altars of state aside for pleasure travel, changed clothes to move incognito, and issued no decree clearing the road or announcing an imperial progress. When the white dragon dresses as a fish, how can officials below tell who stands before them?

sentences.zh: 昔漢光武夜獵，至上東門，守臣郅惲拒弗納，光武以惲能守法而賞之。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Guangwu of Han hunted by night and reached the Upper East Gate; the gatekeeper Zhi Yun refused entry; Guangwu rewarded Yun for upholding the law.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Emperor Guangwu of Han went hunting by night and reached the Upper East Gate. The gatekeeper Zhi Yun refused him entry, and Guangwu rewarded Yun for upholding the law.

sentences.zh: 今小臣欲守郅惲之節，而陛下乃有不敬之誅。

translations.literal: Now this low official wishes to keep Zhi Yun's integrity, yet Your Majesty would impose the penalty for disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: Now this humble official seeks to uphold the same integrity as Zhi Yun, yet Your Majesty would punish that as disrespect.

sentences.zh: 臣恐天下後世以為臣之不幸不若郅惲，陛下寬仁之量亦遠遜光武也。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that under heaven and in later ages men will think an official's misfortune worse than Yun's, and that Your Majesty's measure of clemency falls far short of Guangwu's.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that under heaven and in ages to come people will say an official's misfortune today is worse than Zhi Yun's, and that Your Majesty's measure of mercy falls far short of Emperor Guangwu's.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，帝怒稍解，廷杖六十，釋還，余不問。

translations.literal: ] When the memorial was received the emperor's anger eased somewhat; he was beaten sixty blows in court, released and sent back; the rest were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: ] Once the memorial was received, the emperor's anger eased somewhat. Lin was beaten sixty blows at court, then released and sent home. The others were not questioned.

sentences.zh: 巡撫以下郊迎，禮敬之。

translations.literal: From the governor on down they welcomed him in the suburbs with ceremony and respect.
translations.idiomatic: From the provincial governor on down, officials went out to the suburbs to welcome him with full ceremony and respect.

sentences.zh: 孫清，睢陽諸生也。

translations.literal: Sun Qing was a licentiate of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qing was a licentiate of Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his mother filially.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he served his mother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 母歿未葬，流賊入其境，居民盡逃，清獨守柩不去。

translations.literal: Before his mother was buried, bandits entered the district; residents all fled; Qing alone kept watch by the coffin and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Before his mother could be buried, bandits entered the district and the residents all fled. Qing alone remained to guard the coffin and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 賊兩經其門，皆不入，裏人多賴以全。

translations.literal: Bandits twice passed his gate and did not enter; many in the locality were preserved through him.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits passed his gate twice and did not enter. Many in the neighborhood owed their safety to him.

sentences.zh: 正德九年四月，河南巡按御史江良貴奏聞，並言：「清同邑徐儀女雪梅、嚴清女銳兒皆不受賊汙，憤罵見殺。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Zhengde, Henan investigating censor Jiang Lianggui reported it, and also stated: "Qing's fellow townsman Xu Yi's daughter Xueme and Yan Qing's daughter Ruier all refused to be defiled by bandits and were killed after furious curses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Zhengde, Jiang Lianggui, touring censor of Henan, reported the matter and added: "Sun Qing's fellow townsman Xu Yi's daughter Xueme and Yan Qing's daughter Ruier both refused to be defiled by the bandits and were killed after cursing them in fury.

sentences.zh: 沭陽諸生沈麟以知府劉祥、縣丞程儉為賊所執，挺身詣賊，開陳利害，願以身代。

translations.literal: Shen Lin, licentiate of Shuyang, when Prefect Liu Xiang and Assistant Magistrate Cheng Jian were seized by bandits, stepped forward to the bandits, explained advantage and harm, and offered himself in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Lin, a licentiate of Shuyang, when Prefect Liu Xiang and Assistant Magistrate Cheng Jian were seized by bandits, went straight to the bandits, explained the stakes, and offered himself in their place.

sentences.zh: 賊義之，二人獲釋。

translations.literal: The bandits honored his righteousness; the two men were released.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits respected his righteousness and released the two officials.

sentences.zh: 凡此義烈，有關風化，宜如制旌表。

translations.literal: All such righteous martyrs bear on custom and teaching; they should be honored according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: All such acts of righteous devotion bear on public morals and should be honored with official commendation as the regulations provide.

sentences.zh: 」章下禮官。

translations.literal: ] The memorial was sent down to the rites officials.
translations.idiomatic: ] The memorial was forwarded to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 先是，八年二月，山東巡按御史張璿奏，賊所過州縣，有子救父，婦衛夫，罹賊兵刃者，凡百十九人，皆宜旌表。

translations.literal: Previously, in the second month of the eighth year, Shandong touring censor Zhang Xuan memorialized that in the prefectures and counties through which bandits passed, there were sons saving fathers, wives guarding husbands, and those who suffered under bandit blades—in all 119 persons—all of whom should be honored with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the second month of the eighth year, Zhang Xuan, the touring censor of Shandong, reported that across the prefectures and counties the bandits had traversed, 119 people—including sons who rescued their fathers, wives who shielded their husbands, and others cut down by bandit blades—deserved official recognition.

sentences.zh: 時傅珪代費宏為禮部，言：「所奏人多費廣。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Gui replaced Fei Hong as head of the Ministry of Rites, saying: "The persons reported are too many and the expense too broad."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gui, who had by then succeeded Fei Hong as Minister of Rites, argued that the list was too long and the cost of honoring everyone would be excessive.

sentences.zh: 宜準山西近例，於所在旌善亭側，建二石碑，分書男婦姓名、邑裏及其孝義、貞烈大略，以示旌揚，有司量給殯殮費。

translations.literal: It is fitting to follow the recent Shanxi precedent, building two stone steles beside the local Honor-of-Virtue pavilion, separately inscribing the names of men and women, their districts, and summaries of their filial righteousness and chaste martyrdom, to manifest commendation; officials should apportion burial and encoffining fees as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed following a recent Shanxi model: erect two stone tablets beside each local pavilion of honored virtue, inscribing the names, hometowns, and brief accounts of filial or chaste deeds for men and women alike, and having local officials cover reasonable burial costs.

sentences.zh: 厥後地方有奏，悉以此令從事。

translations.literal: Henceforth wherever localities submitted memorials, all should follow this order in conducting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, local reports of this kind were to be handled solely under this policy.

sentences.zh: 」帝可之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented to it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 至是，良貴奏下，劉春代珪為禮部，竟不請旌，但用珪前議，並給銀建坊之令亦不復行，而旌善之意微矣。

translations.literal: At this point, when Liang Gui's memorial descended, Liu Chun replaced Gui as head of the Ministry of Rites; in the end he did not request commendation, but only used Gui's prior proposal; the order to grant silver for building commemorative arches was also no longer executed, and the intent to honor virtue grew faint.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Liang Gui's report reached the court, Liu Chun had replaced Fu Gui at the Ministry of Rites. Liu declined to seek formal honors altogether, applying only Fu Gui's cheaper stele policy—and even the earlier practice of granting silver for commemorative arches lapsed, so the state's enthusiasm for public virtue visibly cooled.

sentences.zh: 當是時，濮州諸生宋顯章、淅川諸生李豫，皆以孝行著聞，流賊過其門不敢犯，裏人亦多賴以全。

translations.literal: At that time, Puzhou licentiate Song Xianzhang and Xichuan licentiate Li Yu were both famed for filial conduct; roving bandits passing their doors did not dare to violate them, and villagers also largely relied on them to preserve their safety.
translations.idiomatic: Around that time, Song Xianzhang of Puzhou and Li Yu of Xichuan—both licentiates—were known far and wide for filial devotion. Bandits spared their households, and many neighbors owed their lives to their moral standing.

sentences.zh: 而顯章之死也，其妻辛氏自縊以殉。

translations.literal: When Xianzhang died, his wife Lady Xin hanged herself to follow him in martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzhang's death, his wife, Lady Xin, took her own life to join him.

sentences.zh: 知州李緝為建孝節坊，並祠祀。

translations.literal: Prefect Li Jin built a Filial-Chastity arch for them and also enshrined them for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Li Jin erected a memorial arch honoring their filial devotion and chastity, and had them enshrined for veneration.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年，豫獨被旌。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing, Yu alone received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Jiajing reign, only Li Yu received state honors.

sentences.zh: 劉憲，靈石諸生也。

translations.literal: Liu Xian was a Lingshi licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian was a licentiate from Lingshi.

sentences.zh: 父先亡。

translations.literal: His father had died beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: His father had already passed away.

sentences.zh: 母年七十余，兩目俱瞽，憲奉事惟謹。

translations.literal: His mother was over seventy years old, both eyes completely blind; Xian waited upon her with sole devotion.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, blind in both eyes and past seventy, he tended with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 正德六年，流賊入城，憲負母避之城外。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde, roving bandits entered the city; Xian carried his mother on his back to flee outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhengde, when bandits stormed the city, Liu Xian shouldered his mother and fled beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 賊追至，欲殺母，憲哀告曰：「寧殺我，毋害我母。

translations.literal: Bandits pursued and caught up, wishing to kill the mother; Xian pleaded in sorrow, saying: "Better kill me; do not harm my mother."
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits overtook them and moved to kill his mother, Liu Xian begged through tears: "Take my life instead—spare her."

sentences.zh: 」賊乃釋之，行至嶺後，憲竟為他賊所殺。

translations.literal: The bandits then released them; after reaching beyond the ridge, Xian was ultimately killed by other bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits let them go—but beyond the ridge, other raiders killed Liu Xian.

sentences.zh: 賊縱火焚民居，獨憲宅隨爇隨滅。

translations.literal: Bandits set fires burning dwellings; only Xian's house, as it burned, the flames immediately went out.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits torched the neighborhood, yet Xian's house alone seemed to catch fire and then go out as if the flames refused to hold.

sentences.zh: 同時羅璋，遂寧諸生。

translations.literal: At the same time, Luo Zhang, Suining licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same period lived Luo Zhang, a licentiate of Suining.

sentences.zh: 大盜亂蜀中，母為賊所獲，璋手挺長槍，連斃三賊，賊舍母去。

translations.literal: Great robbers stirred chaos in Shu; his mother was seized by bandits; Zhang hand-held a long spear, successively felled three bandits; the bandits released the mother and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When major brigands swept through Sichuan and captured his mother, Luo Zhang took up a long spear, killed three of them in succession, and the rest released her and fled.

sentences.zh: 後賊追至，璋力捍賊，久之力疲，竟被執。

translations.literal: Later bandits pursued and caught up; Zhang forcefully resisted bandits; after long time his strength exhausted, he was ultimately seized.
translations.idiomatic: Pursued again later, he fought until exhaustion and was taken.

sentences.zh: 賊憤甚，剜心剖肝，裂其屍。

translations.literal: Bandits were greatly enraged; they gouged out the heart, dissected the liver, and tore apart his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they cut out his heart and liver and mutilated his body.

sentences.zh: 並正德中旌表。

translations.literal: Both were honored with commendation in the Zhengde period.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were posthumously honored during the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 有李壯丁者，安定縣人。

translations.literal: There was one named Li Zhuangding, a person of Anding County.
translations.idiomatic: One such case was Li Zhuangding of Anding County.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，北寇入犯，從父母奔避山谷。

translations.literal: During Jiajing, northern raiders invaded; following his parents he fled to avoid them in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing era, when northern raiders swept in, he fled with his parents into the hills.

sentences.zh: 遇賊縛母去，壯丁取石奮擊，母得脫。

translations.literal: Encountering bandits who bound his mother and took her away, Zhuangding took stones and struck vigorously; the mother was able to escape.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits seized and bound his mother, Zhuangding pelted them with stones until she broke free.

sentences.zh: 前行復遇五賊，一賊縛其母，母大呼曰：「兒速去，毋顧我！
