translations.literal: Going forward they again encountered five bandits; one bandit bound his mother; the mother cried loudly: "Son, flee quickly; do not care for me!"
translations.idiomatic: Farther on they met five more raiders; one seized his mother, who shouted: "Run, my son—leave me!"

sentences.zh: 」壯丁憤，手提鐵器擊仆賊，母得逃，而壯丁竟為賊所殺。

translations.literal: Zhuangding was enraged; hand-held an iron implement he struck down a bandit; the mother was able to flee, but Zhuangding was ultimately killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, he swung an iron tool and felled one of them—his mother escaped, but the bandits killed him.

sentences.zh: 正德中，賊掠巨鹿，執趙智、趙慧之母，將殺之。

translations.literal: During Zhengde, bandits plundered Julu; they seized the mother of Zhao Zhi and Zhao Hui, about to kill her.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengde era, when bandits raided Julu, they captured the mother of Zhao Zhi and Zhao Hui and were about to execute her.

sentences.zh: 智追至，跪告曰：「母年老，願殺我。

translations.literal: Zhi pursued and caught up; kneeling he pleaded: "Mother is aged; I wish to be killed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhi caught up, knelt, and pleaded: "She is old—kill me instead."

sentences.zh: 」慧亦至，泣曰：「兄年長，願留養母而殺我。

translations.literal: Hui also arrived; weeping she said: "Elder brother is older; I wish to remain to nourish mother and kill me."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hui arrived in tears: "My brother is older and should stay to care for her—take my life."

sentences.zh: 」智方與爭死，而母復請曰：「吾老當死，乞留二子。

translations.literal: Zhi was just contending over dying, while the mother again pleaded: "I am old and ought to die; I beg you spare the two sons."
translations.idiomatic: As the brothers argued over who should die, their mother intervened: "I am old—it is I who should die. Spare my sons."

sentences.zh: 」群賊笑曰：「皆好人也。

translations.literal: The bandits all laughed and said: "All are good people."
translations.idiomatic: The bandits laughed: "What a virtuous family."

sentences.zh: 」並釋之。

translations.literal: And all released them.
translations.idiomatic: Then they released them all.

sentences.zh: 容師偃，香山人。

translations.literal: Rong Shiyan, a person of Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Shiyan came from Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 父患癱疾，扶持不離側。

translations.literal: His father suffered paralytic illness; he supported him and did not leave his side.
translations.idiomatic: His father was paralyzed, and Shiyan never left his side.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年，寇掠其鄉，師偃負父而逃。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengde, raiders plundered his village; Shiyan carried his father on his back and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhengde, when raiders swept his village, he fled carrying his father on his back.

sentences.zh: 追者急，父麾使遁，泣曰：「父子相為命，去將安之。

translations.literal: Pursuers were urgent; the father waved for him to flee, weeping: "Father and son depend on each other for life; if you leave, where will you go?"
translations.idiomatic: With pursuers closing in, his father urged him to flee. Weeping, Shiyan refused: "Our lives are bound together—where would I go without you?"

sentences.zh: 」俄被執，賊灼其父，師偃號泣請代。

translations.literal: Soon they were seized; bandits burned his father; Shiyan wailed and begged to substitute.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon captured; when the bandits set his father alight, Shiyan sobbed and begged to die in his stead.

sentences.zh: 賊從之，父得釋，而師偃焚死。

translations.literal: Bandits assented; the father was released, but Shiyan was burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits accepted; his father was spared, and Shiyan burned to death.

sentences.zh: 後有劉靜者，萬安諸生。

translations.literal: Later there was Liu Jing, a Wan'an licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Liu Jing, a licentiate of Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間，流賊陷其縣，負母出奔。

translations.literal: During Jiajing, roving bandits overran his county; carrying his mother on his back he fled.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits overran Wan'an in the Jiajing era, he shouldered his mother and fled.

sentences.zh: 遇賊，將殺母，靜以身翼蔽求代死。

translations.literal: Encountering bandits, about to kill the mother; Jing with his body winged and covered, seeking to substitute and die.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered by bandits about to kill his mother, he spread his arms to shield her and offered his own life.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，攢刃殺之，猶抱母不解，屍閱七日不變。

translations.literal: Bandits were enraged; gathering blades they killed him; still embracing his mother without releasing; the corpse after seven days showed no change.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they stabbed him to death—yet he clung to his mother even in death, and his body showed no decomposition when examined seven days later.

sentences.zh: 萬歷元年旌表。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli, honored with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: He was officially honored in the first year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 又有溫鉞者，大同人。

translations.literal: There was also Wen Yue, a Datong person.
translations.idiomatic: Another was Wen Yue of Datong.

sentences.zh: 父景清有膽力。

translations.literal: His father Jingqing possessed courage and physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingqing was known for his bravery and strength.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，鎮兵叛，殺巡撫張文錦。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing, garrison troops rebelled, killing Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing, the garrison mutinied and murdered Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin.

sentences.zh: 其後，巡撫蔡天佑令景清密捕首惡，戮數人，其黨恨之。

translations.literal: Thereafter, Grand Coordinator Cai Tianyou ordered Jingqing to secretly capture chief villains; several were executed; their faction hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Grand Coordinator Cai Tianyou sent Jingqing to secretly arrest the ringleaders; several were executed, and the mutineers bore a deep grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 十二年復叛，殺總兵李瑾，因遍索昔年為軍府效命者。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year they rebelled again, killed Regional Commander Li Jin, and consequently searched broadly for those who in former years had served the military administration.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years later they rose again, killed Regional Commander Li Jin, and hunted down everyone who had served the military command years before.

sentences.zh: 景清深匿不出，遂執鉞及其母王氏以去，令言景清所在。

translations.literal: Jingqing hid deeply and did not emerge; they then seized Yue and his mother Lady Wang and took them away, ordering them to speak where Jingqing was.
translations.idiomatic: Jingqing went deep into hiding; the rebels seized Wen Yue and his mother, Lady Wang, and demanded to know Jingqing's whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 鉞曰：「爾欲殺我父，而使我言其處，是我殺父也。

translations.literal: Yue said: "You wish to kill my father, yet make me speak his whereabouts—this would be me killing my father."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yue replied: "You mean to kill my father—and you expect me to betray where he hides? That would make me his murderer."

sentences.zh: 如仇不可解，則殺我舒憤足矣。

translations.literal: If the grudge cannot be resolved, then killing me to vent resentment is sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: If you must have blood, kill me and be done with it.

sentences.zh: 」賊不聽，逼母使言，母大罵不輟。

translations.literal: Bandits would not listen; they forced the mother to speak; the mother cursed loudly without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: They refused. Pressuring his mother to talk, they met only unbroken curses.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，支解以怵鉞。

translations.literal: Bandits were enraged; they dismembered her to intimidate Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, they dismembered her before his eyes to break him.

sentences.zh: 鉞大哭且罵，並被殺。

translations.literal: Yue wept loudly and also cursed; both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yue wept and cursed—and they killed him too.

sentences.zh: 事平，母子並獲旌。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, mother and son both received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, both mother and son were posthumously honored.

sentences.zh: 俞孜，字景修，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Yu Zi, styled Jingxiu, a person of Shanyin, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zi, courtesy name Jingxiu, came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，敦行誼。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate, earnest in conduct and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate, he was known for steadfast integrity and loyalty to friends.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，父華充裏役，解流人徐鐸至口外。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing, his father Hua served as village corvée duty, escorting exile Xu Duo to beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign, his father Hua was pressed into village corvée duty to escort the exiled convict Xu Duo beyond the frontier pass.

sentences.zh: 鐸毒殺華，亡走。

translations.literal: Duo poisoned and killed Hua, then fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Duo poisoned Hua and fled.

sentences.zh: 孜扶櫬歸，誓必報仇，縱跡數十郡不可得。

translations.literal: Zi supported the coffin and returned; he vowed he must avenge; tracking across dozens of prefectures he could not obtain him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zi brought his father's body home and swore vengeance, hunting across dozens of prefectures without success.

sentences.zh: 後聞已還鄉，匿其甥楊氏家。

translations.literal: Later he heard he had returned to his native place, hiding at his nephew Yang's family home.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he learned Xu Duo had slipped back home and was hiding at his nephew's house, the Yang family.

sentences.zh: 乃結力士十數人，佯為賣魚，往來偵伺，且謁知府南大吉乞助。

translations.literal: He then banded together a dozen or so strong men, feigning to sell fish, going back and forth to spy and watch; moreover he visited Prefect Nan Daji to beg assistance.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered a dozen brawny allies, posed as fish sellers to scout the area, and asked Prefect Nan Daji for help.

sentences.zh: 大吉義之，遣數健卒與俱，夜半驟率卒入楊氏家，呼鐸出見，縛送於官，置諸法。

translations.literal: Daji approved of his righteousness; he dispatched several sturdy soldiers to accompany him; at midnight he suddenly led soldiers into the Yang family home, summoned Duo out to appear, bound and sent him to the authorities, and executed him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Nan Daji, moved by his cause, sent armed guards. At midnight they stormed the Yang house, dragged Xu Duo out, bound him, and handed him over for execution.

sentences.zh: 孜自是不復應舉，養繼母以終。

translations.literal: From then on Zi no longer responded to examination summons; he nourished his stepmother to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zi never sat for the examinations again; he devoted himself to caring for his stepmother until her death.

sentences.zh: 有張震者，余姚農家子也。

translations.literal: There was one named Zhang Zhen, a Yuyao farming-family son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhen was a farmer's son from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 生周歲，父為人所陷將死，嚙震指語曰：「某，吾仇也，汝勿忘。

translations.literal: At one year of age, his father was framed by someone and about to die; biting Zhen's finger he said: "So-and-so is my enemy; you must not forget."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhen was one year old, his father, framed and dying, bit the boy's finger and whispered: "Remember this name—he is my enemy."

sentences.zh: 」震長而指瘡不愈，母告以故，震誓必報。

translations.literal: Zhen grew up and the finger sore did not heal; his mother told him the reason; Zhen vowed he must avenge.
translations.idiomatic: The bite left a wound that never healed; when his mother told him why, Zhang Zhen swore he would have revenge.

sentences.zh: 其友謂曰：「汝力弱，吾為汝殺之。

translations.literal: His friend said to him: "You are weak in strength; I will kill him for you."
translations.idiomatic: A friend told him: "You're not strong enough—let me kill him for you."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，仇乘馬出，友以田器擊之，即死。

translations.literal: Before long, the enemy rode out on horseback; the friend with a farm implement struck him; he immediately died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the enemy rode out; the friend felled him with a farm tool, killing him instantly.

sentences.zh: 震喜，走告父墓。

translations.literal: Zhen rejoiced; he ran to tell his father's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Overjoyed, Zhang Zhen ran to his father's grave to report the deed.

sentences.zh: 已而事發，有司傷其誌，減死論戍，遇赦歸。

translations.literal: Before long the matter came to light; officials sympathized with his resolve; death was reduced, sentenced to exile; encountering amnesty he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the killing came to light, officials, moved by his filial motive, commuted the death sentence to exile; he returned home under amnesty.

sentences.zh: 孫文，亦余姚人也。

translations.literal: Sun Wen was also a Yuyao person.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wen, too, was from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 幼時，父為族人時行箠死。

translations.literal: In youth, his father was by clansman Shixing beaten to death with a cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, he watched his father beaten to death by a clansman named Shixing.

sentences.zh: 長欲報之，而力不敵，乃偽與和好，共武斷鄉曲。

translations.literal: Grown, he wished to avenge it, but strength was not equal; he therefore feigned reconciliation and friendship, jointly domineering the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he lacked the strength for open revenge, so he feigned friendship and joined Shixing in bullying their neighbors.

sentences.zh: 時行坦然不復疑。

translations.literal: Shixing was at ease and no longer suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing, trusting him completely, suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 一日，值時行於田間，即以田器擊殺之。

translations.literal: One day, encountering Shixing in the fields, he immediately with a farm implement struck and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: One day he found Shixing alone in the fields and killed him with a farm tool.

sentences.zh: 坐戍，未幾，遇赦獲釋。

translations.literal: Sentenced to exile; before long, encountering amnesty he obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished, but was soon freed by imperial amnesty.

sentences.zh: 崔鑒，京師人。

translations.literal: Cui Jian, a person of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jian was a native of the capital.

sentences.zh: 父嗜酒狎娼，召與居。

translations.literal: His father loved wine and consorted with prostitutes; he summoned Jian to live together.
translations.idiomatic: His father drank heavily, consorted with a courtesan, and made Jian live with them.

sentences.zh: 娼恃寵，時時陵鑒母，父又被酒，數侵辱之。

translations.literal: The prostitute relied on favor; from time to time she bullied Jian's mother; the father, again drunk, repeatedly insulted and humiliated her.
translations.idiomatic: The courtesan, favored by his father, constantly belittled Jian's mother, while his drunken father repeatedly abused her as well.

sentences.zh: 一日，娼惡言詈母，母復之，娼遂擊敗母面。

translations.literal: One day, the prostitute with vicious words cursed the mother; the mother responded in kind; the prostitute then struck and wounded the mother's face.
translations.idiomatic: One day the courtesan reviled his mother; when his mother answered back, the courtesan beat her face bloody.

sentences.zh: 母不勝憤，入室伏床而泣，將自盡。

translations.literal: The mother, unable to bear anger, entered the room, lay prostrate on the bed and wept, about to kill herself.
translations.idiomatic: Overcome with humiliation, his mother retreated to her room, collapsed on the bed in tears, and prepared to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 鑒時年十三，自學舍歸，問之，母告以故。

translations.literal: Jian was then thirteen; returning from the schoolhouse he asked; the mother told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, then thirteen, came home from school, asked what was wrong, and his mother told him everything.

sentences.zh: 鑒曰：「母無死。

translations.literal: Jian said: "Mother, do not die."
translations.idiomatic: "Mother, you must not die," he said.

sentences.zh: 」即走至學舍，挾刃還。

translations.literal: He immediately ran to the schoolhouse, took a blade and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He ran to the school, seized a knife, and came back.

sentences.zh: 娼適掃地，且掃且詈。

translations.literal: The prostitute happened to be sweeping; while sweeping she cursed.
translations.idiomatic: The courtesan was sweeping the floor, muttering curses as she worked.

sentences.zh: 鑒拔刃刺其左脅，立斃，乃匿刃牖下，亡走數里，忽自念曰：「父不知我殺娼，必累我母。

translations.literal: Jian drew the blade and stabbed her left flank; she immediately died; he then hid the blade beneath the window and fled several li; suddenly he thought: "Father does not know I killed the prostitute; he will surely implicate my mother."
translations.idiomatic: He stabbed her in the left side and she fell dead at once. He hid the knife under the window sill and ran several li—then it struck him: if his father did not know he had killed the courtesan, his mother would bear the blame.

sentences.zh: 」急趨歸，父果訴於官，將縶其母矣。

translations.literal: He hurried back; his father had indeed appealed to the authorities; they were about to arrest his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He raced home just as his father had reported the murder to the magistrate, who was about to arrest his mother.

sentences.zh: 鑒至，告捕者曰：「此我所為，非母也。

translations.literal: Jian arrived and told the arresters: "This is what I did; not the mother."
translations.idiomatic: Jian stepped forward and told the officers: "I did this—not my mother."

sentences.zh: 」眾見其幼，不信。

translations.literal: The crowd saw he was young and did not believe him.
translations.idiomatic: No one believed a child could be the killer.

sentences.zh: 鑒曰：「汝等不信，請問兇器安在？

translations.literal: Jian said: "You do not believe; I ask, where is the murder weapon?"
translations.idiomatic: "If you won't believe me," he said, "then tell me—where is the weapon?"

sentences.zh: 」自出刃示之，眾乃釋母，縶鑒置獄。

translations.literal: He himself produced the blade and showed it; the crowd then released the mother and arrested Jian, placing him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: He retrieved the knife and showed it; only then did they release his mother and bind Jian for jail.

sentences.zh: 事聞，下刑部讞。

translations.literal: The matter was reported; it was sent down to the Ministry of Punishments for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When news reached the court, the case was referred to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 尚書聞淵等議，鑒誌在救母，且年少可矜，難拘常律。

translations.literal: Minister Wen Yuan and others deliberated: Jian's intent was to save his mother, and moreover he was young and pitiable; ordinary statutes were hard to apply strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wen Yuan and his colleagues noted that Jian had acted to save his mother, that he was young and deserving of sympathy, and that strict application of the usual penalty would be unjust.

sentences.zh: 帝亦貸其罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor also pardoned his crime.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned him as well.

sentences.zh: 唐儼，全州諸生也。

translations.literal: Tang Yan was a Quanzhou licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yan was a licentiate from Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父蔭，郴州知州，歸老得危疾。

translations.literal: His father Yin was Chenzhou prefect; retiring in old age he contracted a grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin, former prefect of Chenzhou, fell gravely ill after retiring.

sentences.zh: 儼年十二，潛割臂肉進之，疾良已。

translations.literal: Yan was twelve; secretly he cut arm flesh and presented it; the illness was soon cured.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve, Yan secretly cut flesh from his own arm and fed it to his father, who soon recovered.

sentences.zh: 及父歿，哀毀如成人。

translations.literal: When his father died, grief and devastation were like an adult's.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he mourned with the sorrow of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 其後遊學於外，嫡母寢疾。

translations.literal: Afterward he went to study abroad, and his stepmother fell ill and took to bed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while he was away studying, his stepmother fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 儼妻鄧氏年十八，奮曰：「吾婦人，安知湯藥。

translations.literal: Yan's wife, née Deng, aged eighteen, roused herself and said: "I am a woman—how would I know medicines and decoctions?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan's wife, Lady Deng, was eighteen. With sudden resolve she said, "I am only a woman—what do I know of medicines and brews?"

sentences.zh: 昔夫子以臂肉療吾舅，吾獨不能療吾姑哉？

translations.literal: In the past my husband cut flesh from his arm to cure my father-in-law; am I alone unable to cure my mother-in-law?"
translations.idiomatic: Once my husband cut flesh from his own arm to heal his father—is it beyond me to heal my mother-in-law?"

sentences.zh: 」於是割脅肉以進，姑疾亦愈。

translations.literal: Thereupon she cut flesh from her side and presented it; her mother-in-law's illness was also cured.
translations.idiomatic: So she cut flesh from her own side and fed it to her. The stepmother recovered.

sentences.zh: 儼聞母疾，馳歸，則無恙久矣，拜其妻曰：「此吾分也，當急召我，何自苦如此！

translations.literal: Yan heard of his mother's illness and galloped home; she had been well for some time already. He bowed to his wife and said: "This was my duty—you should have urgently summoned me; why did you afflict yourself so!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yan heard his mother was ill, he raced home—but she had already been well for some time. He bowed to his wife and said, "That was my duty. You should have sent for me at once. Why put yourself through such suffering?"

sentences.zh: 」妻曰：「子事父，婦事姑，一也。

translations.literal: His wife said: "A son serves his father; a wife serves her mother-in-law—it is the same."
translations.idiomatic: His wife replied, "A son serves his father; a wife serves her mother-in-law. The obligation is the same."

sentences.zh: 方危急時，召子何及。

translations.literal: When crisis is at hand, summoning a son—what use is there?"
translations.idiomatic: In a crisis, by the time you can send for a son, it is already too late."

sentences.zh: 且事必待子，安用婦為。

translations.literal: Besides, if every matter must wait for a son, what need is there for a wife?"
translations.idiomatic: And if every duty must wait for a son, what is a wife for?"

sentences.zh: 」儼益嘆異。

translations.literal: Yan was all the more astonished and admired her.
translations.idiomatic: Yan marveled at her all the more.

sentences.zh: 嫡母歿二十年，而生母歿，儼廬墓三年。

translations.literal: Twenty years after his stepmother died, when his birth mother died, Yan lived in a hut by the tomb for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years after his stepmother's death, when his birth mother died, Yan mourned at her grave in a hut for three years.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年貢至京，有司奏旌其門。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 4, recommended as tribute student he reached the capital; the authorities memorialized to commend his household gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 4 he was sent to the capital as a tribute student; the local authorities memorialized the throne, and his family received an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 丘緒，字繼先，鄞縣諸生他。

translations.literal: Qiu Xu, styled Jixian, was a Yinxian licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Xu, courtesy name Jixian, was a licentiate of Yinxian County.

sentences.zh: 生母黃，為嫡余所逐，適江東包氏。

translations.literal: His birth mother Huang was driven out by the principal wife Yu and married into the Bao clan east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: His birth mother, surnamed Huang, had been driven out by the principal wife, Lady Yu, and remarried to the Bao family east of the river.

sentences.zh: 未幾轉適他所，遂不復相聞。

translations.literal: Before long she married elsewhere again; thereafter they no longer had contact.
translations.idiomatic: She soon married again elsewhere, and contact was lost entirely.

sentences.zh: 緒年十五，父歿，事余至孝。

translations.literal: Xu was fifteen when his father died; he served Yu with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Xu was fifteen when his father died; he served Lady Yu with exceptional devotion.

sentences.zh: 余疾，謹奉湯藥，不解衣帶者數月。

translations.literal: When Yu fell ill, he dutifully attended with medicines and broth, not removing clothes or belt for several months.
translations.idiomatic: When she fell ill, he nursed her with medicines, never changing clothes or loosening his belt for months on end.

sentences.zh: 余重感其孝，病革，與訣曰：「我即死，汝無忘若母。

translations.literal: Yu was deeply moved by his filial piety; at the crisis of illness she took leave, saying: "When I die, do not forget your mother."
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved by his devotion, Lady Yu, on her deathbed, bid him farewell: "When I am gone, do not forget your own mother."

sentences.zh: 」時母被逐已二十年矣。

translations.literal: At that time his mother had been driven out twenty years already.
translations.idiomatic: By then his mother had been cast out twenty years earlier.

sentences.zh: 一夕，夢人告曰：「若母在臺州金鰲寺前。

translations.literal: One night a person in a dream told him: "Your mother is before Jin'ao Temple in Taizhou."
translations.idiomatic: One night a figure appeared in his dream and said, "Your mother is at Jin'ao Temple in Taizhou."

sentences.zh: 」覺而識之。

translations.literal: Waking, he remembered it.
translations.idiomatic: He woke and fixed the words in his mind.

sentences.zh: 次日，與一人憩於途，詰之，則包氏故養馬廝也。

translations.literal: The next day he rested on the road with a man; questioning him, it turned out to be a former horse groom of the Bao clan.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he rested on the road with a stranger and, questioning him, found he had once been a groom in the Bao household.

sentences.zh: 叩以母所向，曰：「有周平者曾悉其事，今已戍京衛矣。

translations.literal: Asked where his mother had gone, the man said: "One Zhou Ping once knew the whole affair; he is now garrisoned in the capital guard."
translations.idiomatic: When Xu asked after his mother's whereabouts, the man said, "A man named Zhou Ping once knew the whole story; he is now serving in the capital garrison."

sentences.zh: 」緒姊婿謁選在京，遺書囑訪平，久之未得。

translations.literal: Xu's sister's husband was in the capital for official selection; Xu sent a letter instructing him to seek out Ping, but after a long time he was not found.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's brother-in-law was in the capital awaiting appointment; Xu wrote asking him to find Zhou Ping, but months passed without success.

sentences.zh: 一日，有避雨於邸門者，其聲類鄞人，叩之，即周平也，言黃已適臺州李副使子。

translations.literal: One day someone sheltering from rain at a lodge gate had a voice like a Yin native; questioned, it was Zhou Ping, who said Huang had married the son of Vice Commissioner Li of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: One day a man sheltering from rain at an inn gate spoke with a Yin accent. Xu questioned him—it was Zhou Ping, who said Huang had married the son of Vice Commissioner Li of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 緒得報，即之臺，而李已歿，其嗣子漫不知前事。

translations.literal: Xu got the report and went at once to Taizhou; but Li was already dead, and his heir knew nothing at all of earlier matters.
translations.idiomatic: Xu set out for Taizhou at once, but Li was already dead and his heir knew nothing of the past.

sentences.zh: 緒仿徨掩泣於道，有傷之者，導謁老媒妁王四，曰已再適仙居吳義官。

translations.literal: Xu wandered about the road, covering his face and weeping; one who took pity on him led him to the old matchmaker Wang Si, who said she had remarried Assistant Commander Wu of Xianju.
translations.idiomatic: Xu wandered the road weeping; a passerby took pity and brought him to an old matchmaker, Wang Si, who said Huang had remarried to Assistant Commander Wu of Xianju.

sentences.zh: 吳，仙居巨族也。

translations.literal: The Wu were a great clan of Xianju.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu were a leading family in Xianju.

sentences.zh: 緒至，歷間數十家，無所遇。

translations.literal: Xu arrived and inquired at dozens of households; he found nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu arrived and knocked on dozens of doors without finding her.

sentences.zh: 已而抵一儒生吳秉朗家，語之故。

translations.literal: Before long he reached the home of the scholar Wu Binglang and told him the whole matter.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he came to the home of a scholar, Wu Binglang, and told him the whole story.

sentences.zh: 生感其意，留止焉。

translations.literal: The scholar was moved by his purpose and kept him there.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by Xu's purpose, Wu Binglang took him in.

sentences.zh: 有叔母聞所留者異鄉人也，恚而咻之。

translations.literal: An aunt heard the one being lodged was a man from another region and, furious, drove him out with curses.
translations.idiomatic: An aunt heard that Wu was sheltering a stranger and, enraged, drove Xu out with curses.

sentences.zh: 生告以緒意。

translations.literal: The scholar told her of Xu's purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Binglang explained Xu's quest to her.

sentences.zh: 叔母者，黃故主母也，頗憶前事，然不詳所往。

translations.literal: The aunt was Huang's former mistress; she remembered the earlier matter rather well, but did not know clearly where she had gone.
translations.idiomatic: That aunt had once been Huang's mistress; she remembered much of the past but could not say where Huang had gone.

sentences.zh: 呼舊蒼頭問之，雲金鰲寺前，去歲經之，棺已殯寺旁矣。

translations.literal: She called an old manservant to ask; he said Jin'ao Temple front—passing there last year, a coffin had already been entombed beside the temple.
translations.idiomatic: She summoned an old retainer, who said, "Jin'ao Temple"—he had passed there the year before and a coffin had already been laid to rest beside the temple.

sentences.zh: 緒以其言與夢合，信之，行且泣，牛觸之墜於溝，則輿夫馬長之門也。

translations.literal: Xu, believing the words matched his dream, walked weeping; an ox butted him and he fell into a ditch—it was at the gate of the litter-bearer Ma Changzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced the account matched his dream, Xu walked on weeping. An ox knocked him into a ditch outside the home of Ma Changzhi, a sedan-chair bearer.

sentences.zh: 駭而出，問所從來。

translations.literal: Startled, Ma came out and asked whence he came.
translations.idiomatic: Ma rushed out in alarm and asked where he had come from.

sentences.zh: 緒以情告。

translations.literal: Xu told him the full circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: Xu told him the whole story.

sentences.zh: 長曰：「吾前輿一婦至縉雲蒼嶺下，殆是也。

translations.literal: Ma said: "I previously carried a woman to below Cangling in Jinyun—that is probably she."
translations.idiomatic: Ma said, "I once carried a woman down to Cangling below Jinyun—that may be her."

sentences.zh: 」輿緒至其處。

translations.literal: He carried Xu in a litter to that place.
translations.idiomatic: He took Xu there in his chair.

sentences.zh: 緒遍物色，無所遇，倀倀行委巷中。

translations.literal: Xu searched everywhere and found nothing; disconsolate, he walked in winding lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Xu searched everywhere without success and wandered lost through back alleys.

sentences.zh: 一媼立門外，探之，知為鄞人，告以所從來。

translations.literal: An old woman stood outside a gate; he tested her and learned she was from Yin; he told her whence he came.
translations.idiomatic: An old woman stood at a doorway. Probing her accent, he found she was from Yin and told her why he had come.

sentences.zh: 嫗亦轉詢丘氏耗，則緒母也。

translations.literal: The old woman in turn asked news of the Qiu clan—it was Xu's mother.
translations.idiomatic: The old woman, in turn, asked for news of the Qiu family—it was his mother.

sentences.zh: 抱持而哭，閭裏皆感動。

translations.literal: They embraced and wept; the whole neighborhood was moved.
translations.idiomatic: They embraced and wept until every neighbor was moved.

sentences.zh: 寺旁棺者，蓋其姒氏雲。

translations.literal: The coffin beside the temple was, it turned out, her elder sister-in-law's.
translations.idiomatic: The coffin beside the temple, it turned out, belonged to her sister-in-law.

sentences.zh: 所適陳翁，貧而無子，且多負。

translations.literal: The man she had married, Old Man Chen, was poor and without sons, and moreover deep in debt.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband, Old Chen, was poor, childless, and heavily in debt.

sentences.zh: 緒還取金償之，並迎翁以歸，備極孝養。

translations.literal: Xu returned to fetch gold to repay the debts, and also brought the old man home, supporting him with utmost filial care.
translations.idiomatic: Xu went home for money to pay off the debts, brought Old Chen back with him, and cared for both his mother and her husband with every devotion.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年，知縣趙民順入覲，疏聞於朝，獲旌表。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 14, Magistrate Zhao Minshun went to audience at court and memorialized the matter; he received an official commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 14, Magistrate Zhao Minshun memorialized the throne during his audience at court, and Xu received an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 張鈞，石州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun was a man of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was a man of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 父赦，國子生。

translations.literal: His father She was a student of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: His father She was a student of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 以二親早亡，矢誌不仕，隱居城北村。

translations.literal: Because both parents died early, he vowed never to take office and lived in seclusion in a village north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Both parents having died young, he vowed never to serve in office and lived in seclusion in a village north of the city.

sentences.zh: 鈞，正德末舉於鄉。

translations.literal: Jun passed the provincial examination at the end of the Zhengde reign.
translations.idiomatic: Jun passed the provincial examination near the end of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 以親老亦不仕，讀書養親，遠近皆稱其孝。

translations.literal: Because his parents were old he also did not take office; he read books and supported his parents—near and far all praised his filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His parents now being old, he again declined office, devoting himself to study and their care; near and far, all praised his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十年，俺答犯石州。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 20, Altan raided Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 20, Altan Khan raided Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 鈞慮父遭難，自城中馳一騎號泣赴救。

translations.literal: Jun feared his father would meet disaster; from the city he galloped a single horse, weeping and wailing, to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his father, Jun mounted a horse in the city and rode out weeping to save him.

sentences.zh: 寇射中其肩，裹瘡疾馳，至則父已被殺。

translations.literal: The raiders shot him in the shoulder; he bound the wound and galloped on, but when he arrived his father had already been killed.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders shot him in the shoulder; he bound the wound and rode on, but when he arrived his father was already dead.

sentences.zh: 鈞隕絕，盡餂父血，水漿不入口三日，不勝悲痛而卒。

translations.literal: Jun fainted dead away, licked up all his father's blood, took neither water nor gruel for three days, and died unable to bear the grief.
translations.idiomatic: Jun collapsed senseless, licked his father's blood from the ground, took neither water nor food for three days, and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 越二年，有司上其狀，獲旌。

translations.literal: Two years later the authorities submitted his record and he received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the authorities submitted his case, and he received an official commendation.

sentences.zh: 是時殺掠甚慘，石州為親死者十一人，而張承相、於博、張永安尤著。

translations.literal: At that time the killing and looting were very grim; eleven men in Shizhou died for their parents, and Zhang Chengxiang, Yu Bo, and Zhang Yong'an were especially notable.
translations.idiomatic: The slaughter and looting were terrible; eleven men in Shizhou died defending their parents, but Zhang Chengxiang, Yu Bo, and Zhang Yong'an were especially remembered.

sentences.zh: 承相少孤，及長為諸生，養母二十余年，以孝聞。

translations.literal: Chengxiang was orphaned young; when grown he became a licentiate and supported his mother for more than twenty years, famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiang lost his father young; as a grown licentiate he supported his mother for more than twenty years and was known for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 寇至，負母出逃，為所得，叩頭號泣，乞免其母。

translations.literal: When raiders came he carried his mother on his back to flee; they were seized; he kowtowed and wailed, begging them to spare his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders came he fled with his mother on his back; they were caught, and he kowtowed and wept, begging them to spare her.

sentences.zh: 寇怒，並殺之，抱母首死。

translations.literal: The raiders in anger killed them both; he died still embracing his mother's head.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the raiders killed them both; he died still holding his mother's severed head.

sentences.zh: 博二歲而孤，奉母盡孝。

translations.literal: Bo was orphaned at two and served his mother with complete filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was orphaned at two and devoted himself entirely to his mother.

sentences.zh: 寇抵城下，博方讀書城中。

translations.literal: Raiders reached the foot of the city wall; Bo was then studying in the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders reached the city walls, Bo was studying inside the town.

sentences.zh: 母居村舍，亟下城號泣求母。

translations.literal: His mother lived in a village dwelling; he hurried down from the city wailing and seeking his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His mother lived in a village outside the walls; he rushed down from the city, weeping and searching for her.

sentences.zh: 母已被執，遇諸途，博取石奮擊寇。

translations.literal: His mother had already been seized; meeting them on the road, Bo took up a stone and struck fiercely at the raiders.
translations.idiomatic: She had already been seized; he met them on the road, seized a stone, and struck at the raiders with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 寇就剖其心，母得逸去，年止十有八。

translations.literal: The raiders at once cut open his chest; his mother escaped; he was only eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders cut out his heart on the spot; his mother escaped. He was only eighteen.

sentences.zh: 永安，石州吏也。

translations.literal: Yong'an was a clerk of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an was a clerk of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 父為寇所逐，永安持梃追擊之，傷二賊，趣父逸去，而身自後衛之，被數十創死。

translations.literal: His father was pursued by raiders; Yong'an took a club and chased after them, wounding two bandits, urging his father to flee while he himself guarded the rear, and died from dozens of wounds.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders pursued his father, Yong'an took a club and chased them, wounding two; he urged his father to flee, covered the retreat himself, and died of dozens of wounds.

sentences.zh: 與鈞同被旌。

translations.literal: He received commendation together with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He received an official commendation together with Jun.

sentences.zh: 有溫繼宗者，沁州諸生。

translations.literal: There was Wen Jizong, a licentiate of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was Wen Jizong, a licentiate of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 父卒，不能葬，日守柩哀泣。

translations.literal: His father died; unable to bury him, he daily kept watch beside the coffin in grief and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he could not afford a burial and kept daily vigil beside the coffin, weeping in grief.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十一年，寇入犯，或勸出城避難，以父殯不肯去。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 21 raiders invaded; some urged him to leave the city to escape, but because his father's coffin lay unburied he refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 21 raiders invaded; others urged him to flee the city, but with his father's coffin still unburied he would not leave.

sentences.zh: 寇至，與叔父淵等力禦，擊傷一賊，中矢死柩旁，淵等皆死。

translations.literal: Raiders arrived; with his uncle Yuan and others he resisted with all his strength, wounding one bandit; he was struck by an arrow and died beside the coffin, and Yuan and the others all died.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders came he fought beside his uncle Yuan and the others, wounding one bandit; struck by an arrow, he died beside the coffin, and Yuan and the rest perished as well.

sentences.zh: 亦與鈞同被旌。

translations.literal: He too received commendation together with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He too received an official commendation together with Jun.

sentences.zh: 王在復，太倉人。

translations.literal: Wang Zaifu was a man of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zaifu was a man of Taicang.

sentences.zh: 年二十一，從父讀書城外。

translations.literal: At twenty-one he was studying with his father outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-one he was studying with his father outside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 倭寇入犯，父子亟奔入城。

translations.literal: Wokou invaded; father and son hurried to rush into the city.
translations.idiomatic: When wokou raiders struck, father and son rushed toward the city.

sentences.zh: 父體肥不能速行，中道遇賊，遂相失。

translations.literal: His father was corpulent and could not go quickly; midway they met bandits and thus became separated.
translations.idiomatic: His father was heavyset and could not keep pace; they met bandits on the road and were separated.

sentences.zh: 在復走二里許，展轉尋父。

translations.literal: Zaifu went about two li, turning back and forth seeking his father.
translations.idiomatic: Zaifu ran nearly two li, doubling back again and again in search of his father.

sentences.zh: 聞父被執，急趨賊所，叩頭求免。

translations.literal: Hearing his father had been seized, he hurried to the bandits' place and kowtowed begging for his release.
translations.idiomatic: Learning his father had been seized, he rushed to the bandits and kowtowed, begging for his life.

sentences.zh: 賊不聽，拔刃擬其父，在復以身蔽之，痛哭哀求。

translations.literal: The bandits would not listen; drawing blades they made to strike his father; Zaifu shielded him with his body, weeping bitterly and pleading.
translations.idiomatic: They would not listen. When they drew their blades against his father, Zaifu threw himself between them, weeping and pleading.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，並殺之，兩首墜地，而手猶抱父不釋。

translations.literal: The bandits in anger killed them both; both heads fell to the ground, yet his hands still clutched his father and would not let go.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the bandits killed them both. Both heads fell to the ground, yet Zaifu's arms still clung to his father.

sentences.zh: 時嘉靖三十三年五月也。

translations.literal: It was the fifth month of Jiajing 33.
translations.idiomatic: It was the fifth month of Jiajing 33.

sentences.zh: 當是時，倭亂東南，孝子以衛父母見殺者甚眾，其得旌於朝者，在復及黃巖王蒐、慈谿向敘、無錫蔡元銳、丹徒殷士望。

translations.literal: At that time, with wokou turmoil in the southeast, filial sons who died defending their parents were very many; those who received commendation at court were Zaifu, Wang Sou of Huangyan, Xiang Xu of Cixi, Cai Yuanrui of Wuxi, and Yin Shiwang of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: In those years wokou ravaged the southeast, and many filial sons died defending their parents; those officially commended at court included Zaifu, Wang Sou of Huangyan, Xiang Xu of Cixi, Cai Yuanrui of Wuxi, and Yin Shiwang of Dantu.

sentences.zh: 蒐隨父顯避賊。

translations.literal: Sou followed his father Xian in fleeing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sou fled with his father Xian to escape the raiders.

sentences.zh: 顯被執，將殺之。

translations.literal: Xian was seized and about to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was seized and about to be killed.

sentences.zh: 蒐亟趨前請代，賊遂殺蒐而釋顯。

translations.literal: Sou hurried forward and asked to take his place; the bandits then killed Sou and released Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Sou rushed forward and offered himself in his father's place; the bandits killed Sou and let Xian go.

sentences.zh: 敘為慈谿諸生。

translations.literal: Xu was a licentiate of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was a licentiate of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 倭入寇，以縣無城，掖母出避。

translations.literal: When wokou invaded, the county had no walls; he supported his mother under the arm and went out to flee.
translations.idiomatic: When wokou raiders came, the county had no walls; he supported his mother under the arm and fled.

sentences.zh: 遇賊，踣敘而斫其母，敘急起抱母頸，大呼曰：「寧殺我，毋殺我母！

translations.literal: They met bandits, who knocked Xu down and hacked at his mother; Xu quickly rose and embraced his mother's neck, crying out: "Better kill me—do not kill my mother!"
translations.idiomatic: They met bandits, who knocked Xu down and hacked at his mother. He sprang up, threw his arms around her neck, and cried, "Kill me instead—spare my mother!"

sentences.zh: 」賊如其言，母獲全。

translations.literal: The bandits did as he said; his mother was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits did as he asked, and his mother was spared.

sentences.zh: 俱嘉靖三十五年旌表。

translations.literal: All were commended in Jiajing 35.
translations.idiomatic: All were officially commended in Jiajing 35.

sentences.zh: 元銳，無錫人，與弟元鐸並孝友。

translations.literal: Yuanrui was a man of Wuxi; with his younger brother Yuanduo he was noted for filial piety and brotherly regard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrui was from Wuxi; he and his younger brother Yuanduo were known for filial devotion and brotherly love.

sentences.zh: 倭犯無錫，入元銳家，兄弟急扶父升屋避匿。

translations.literal: Wokou raided Wuxi and entered Yuanrui's home; the brothers urgently helped their father up onto the roof to hide.
translations.idiomatic: When wokou raiders struck Wuxi and entered their home, the brothers hurried their father onto the roof to hide.

sentences.zh: 而元銳為賊執，令言父所在，堅不從，遂見殺。

translations.literal: But Yuanrui was seized by bandits and ordered to reveal where his father was; he steadfastly refused and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanrui was seized and ordered to reveal his father's hiding place; he refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 元鐸不知兄死，明日持重貲往贖，並見殺。

translations.literal: Yuanduo did not know his brother was dead; the next day he brought heavy ransom and was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanduo, not knowing his brother was dead, came the next day with a heavy ransom and was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年旌表。

translations.literal: Commended in Jiajing 38.
translations.idiomatic: They received an official commendation in Jiajing 38.

sentences.zh: 士望，丹徒人，事親孝。

translations.literal: Shiwang was a man of Dantu; he served his parents filially.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwang was from Dantu and served his parents with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 倭犯京口，父被掠，士望請代死。

translations.literal: When wokou raided Jingkou, his father was captured; Shiwang asked to die in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When wokou raiders struck Jingkou and seized his father, Shiwang offered to die in his place.

sentences.zh: 賊笑而試之，火炙刀刺，受之怡然，賊兩釋之。

translations.literal: The bandits laughed and tested him—with fire and blade he endured it calmly; the bandits released them both.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits laughed and tested him with fire and blade; he bore it without flinching, and they released them both.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十三年旌表。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 43, official commendation was granted.
translations.idiomatic: They received official commendation in Jiajing 43.

sentences.zh: 其他未及旌表者，又有陳經孚、龔可正、伍民憲。

translations.literal: Among others not yet commended, there were also Chen Jingfu, Gong Kezheng, and Wu Minxian.
translations.idiomatic: Others not yet officially commended included Chen Jingfu, Gong Kezheng, and Wu Minxian.

sentences.zh: 經孚，平陽人。

translations.literal: Jingfu was a man of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfu was from Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 倭至，負母出逃，遇賊索母珥環，欲殺之。

translations.literal: When wokou arrived, he carried his mother on his back and fled; he met bandits who demanded his mother's ear ornaments and meant to kill her.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders came, he fled carrying his mother on his back. Bandits intercepted them, demanding his mother's earrings and threatening to kill her.

sentences.zh: 經孚以身翼蔽，賊怒，揮刃截耳及肩而死，手猶抱母頸不解。

translations.literal: Jingfu shielded her with his body like wings; the bandits grew angry, swung their blades and cut off his ear and shoulder, killing him, yet his hands still embraced his mother's neck and did not loosen.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfu spread his body to shield her. Enraged, the bandits slashed him, cutting off his ear and deep into his shoulder. He died with his arms still locked around his mother's neck.

sentences.zh: 可正，嘉定諸生。

translations.literal: Kezheng was a licentiate of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Kezheng, a student of Jiading, held licentiate status.

sentences.zh: 負祖母避賊，天雨泥濘，猝遇賊。

translations.literal: Carrying his grandmother on his back to flee bandits, it rained and the mud was thick; he suddenly met bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He was carrying his grandmother to escape the raiders when rain turned the roads to mud. Suddenly bandits appeared.

sentences.zh: 賊惡見婦人，欲殺其祖母，叱可正去。

translations.literal: The bandits hated seeing women and wished to kill his grandmother, ordering Kezheng to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits hated encountering women and meant to kill his grandmother. They ordered Kezheng away.

sentences.zh: 可正跪泣請代，賊不從。

translations.literal: Kezheng knelt weeping and asked to take her place; the bandits would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Kezheng knelt and wept, begging to die in her place. The bandits refused.

sentences.zh: 可正以身覆祖母，賊並殺之。

translations.literal: Kezheng covered his grandmother with his body; the bandits killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: Kezheng threw himself over his grandmother. The bandits killed them both.

sentences.zh: 民憲，晉江人。

translations.literal: Minxian was a man of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Minxian was from Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 扶父避難，遇賊，長跪哀告曰：「勿驚我父，他物任取之。

translations.literal: Supporting his father to flee disaster, he met bandits, knelt long and pleaded mournfully: "Do not frighten my father—take whatever else you wish."
translations.idiomatic: He was helping his father flee when they met bandits. He dropped to his knees and pleaded, "Please don't frighten my father. Take whatever else you want."

sentences.zh: 」賊不聽，竟殺其父。

translations.literal: The bandits would not listen and in the end killed his father.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits paid no heed and killed his father.

sentences.zh: 民憲憤，挺身殺二賊，傷數賊。

translations.literal: Minxian grew furious, sprang forward and killed two bandits, wounding several others.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Minxian sprang up and killed two raiders, wounding several more.

sentences.zh: 賊至益多，斷民憲右手。

translations.literal: As bandits arrived in ever greater numbers, they severed Minxian's right hand.
translations.idiomatic: More raiders arrived and cut off Minxian's right hand.

sentences.zh: 臥草中，猶一手執戈，呼其父三日而絕。

translations.literal: Lying in the grass, he still held a halberd in one hand, calling out to his father for three days before dying.
translations.idiomatic: He lay in the grass, still gripping a halberd in his remaining hand, calling to his father for three days until he died.

sentences.zh: 夏子孝，字以忠，桐城人。

translations.literal: Xia Zixiao, courtesy name Yizhong, was a man of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Zixiao, styled Yizhong, was from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 六歲失母，哀哭如成人。

translations.literal: At six he lost his mother and mourned weeping like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother at six and wept in grief like a grown man.

sentences.zh: 九歲父得危疾，禱天地，刲股六寸許，調羹以進，父食之頓愈。

translations.literal: At nine his father contracted a grave illness; he prayed to Heaven and Earth, cut flesh from his thigh about six inches, prepared broth and presented it, and when his father ate it he recovered at once.
translations.idiomatic: At nine, when his father fell gravely ill, he prayed to Heaven and Earth, cut six inches of flesh from his thigh, made broth and fed it to him. His father recovered immediately.

sentences.zh: 翌日，子孝痛創，父詰其故，始知之。

translations.literal: The next day Zixiao's wound pained him; his father questioned the cause and only then learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when the wound pained him, his father pressed him for an explanation and only then learned what he had done.

sentences.zh: 裏老以聞於官，知府胡麟先夢王祥來謁，詰旦而縣牒至，詫曰：「孺子其祥後身耶？

translations.literal: The village elder reported it to the authorities; Prefect Hu Linxian dreamed that Wang Xiang came to pay a visit, and at dawn the county dispatch arrived; he marveled and said: "Could this lad be the reincarnation of Xiang?"
translations.idiomatic: The village elder reported the matter to the authorities. Prefect Hu Linxian dreamed that Wang Xiang came to visit him; at dawn a county report arrived. Astonished, he said, "Could this boy be Wang Xiang reborn?"

sentences.zh: 」召見，易其舊名「恩」曰「子孝」。

translations.literal: He summoned him for an audience and changed his old name "En" to "Zixiao."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the boy and changed his name from En to Zixiao—"Filial Son."

sentences.zh: 督學御史胡植即令入學為諸生，月廩之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief of Education Hu Zhi immediately ordered him enrolled as a licentiate and granted him monthly stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Education Censor Hu Zhi immediately enrolled him as a licentiate and awarded him a monthly stipend.

sentences.zh: 麟復屬貢士趙簡授之經。

translations.literal: Linxian further entrusted tribute student Zhao Jian to teach him the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linxian also entrusted a tribute student, Zhao Jian, to instruct him in the classics.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末，父卒，廬墓，獨居荒山，身無完衣，形容槁瘁。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiajing his father died; he lived in a hut by the tomb, dwelling alone on a barren mountain, with no whole garment on his body, his form withered and haggard.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jiajing reign his father died. He mourned at the grave in a hut on a desolate hillside, alone, in ragged clothes, his body wasted and gaunt.

sentences.zh: 後歷事王畿、羅汝芳、史桂芳、耿定向，獲聞聖賢之學。

translations.literal: Later he successively studied under Wang Ji, Luo Rufang, Shi Guifang, and Geng Dingxiang, and came to hear the learning of sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied under Wang Ji, Luo Rufang, Shi Guifang, and Geng Dingxiang, and came to know the teachings of the sages.

sentences.zh: 定向為督學御史，將疏聞於朝，固辭曰：「不肖不忍以亡親賈名。

translations.literal: Dingxiang served as education censor and was about to memorialize the court on his behalf; he firmly declined, saying: "Your unworthy servant cannot bear to trade on a dead parent for fame."
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Dingxiang, as education censor, was about to memorialize the throne on his behalf, he firmly refused: "I cannot bear to gain renown at the price of my dead father's grief."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was dropped.

sentences.zh: 將死，命其子曰：「葬我父墓側。」

translations.literal: As he was about to die, he instructed his son: "Bury me beside my father's tomb."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his son, "Bury me beside my father's grave."

sentences.zh: 阿寄者，淳安徐氏仆也。

translations.literal: A Ji was a servant of the Xu family of Chun'an.
translations.idiomatic: A Ji was a servant in the Xu household of Chun'an.

sentences.zh: 徐氏昆弟析產而居，伯得一馬，仲得一牛，季寡婦得阿寄，時年五十余矣。

translations.literal: The Xu brothers divided their property and lived apart; the eldest got a horse, the second an ox, and the youngest brother's widow got A Ji, who was then over fifty.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu brothers divided the estate: the eldest took a horse, the second an ox, and the youngest brother's widow was left with A Ji, then past fifty.

sentences.zh: 寡婦泣曰：「馬則乘，牛則耕，老仆何益。

translations.literal: The widow wept and said: "A horse one rides, an ox one plows with—what use is an old servant?"
translations.idiomatic: The widow wept and said, "A horse you ride, an ox you plow with—what good is an old servant?"

sentences.zh: 」寄嘆曰：「主謂我不若牛馬耶！

translations.literal: Ji sighed and said: "Does my mistress think me inferior to ox and horse!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji sighed and said, "Does my mistress think I'm worth less than cattle?"

sentences.zh: 」乃畫策營生，示可用狀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he devised plans to earn a living and showed what he could do.
translations.idiomatic: So he made plans to earn their keep and proved his worth.

sentences.zh: 寡婦盡脫簪珥，得白金十二兩，畀寄。

translations.literal: The widow removed all her hairpins and earrings, obtained twelve taels of silver, and gave them to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The widow sold every hairpin and earring she had, raised twelve taels of silver, and gave them to Ji.

sentences.zh: 寄入山販漆，期年而三倍其息，謂寡婦曰：「主無憂，富可致矣。

translations.literal: Ji went into the mountains to trade lacquer; within a year he tripled the principal and told the widow: "Mistress, do not worry—wealth can be attained."
translations.idiomatic: Ji went into the hills to trade lacquer. Within a year he had tripled the capital. "Don't worry, mistress," he said. "We can be rich."

sentences.zh: 」歷二十年，積資巨萬，為寡婦嫁三女，婚二子，賫聘皆千金。

translations.literal: Over twenty years he amassed capital in the tens of thousands, married off three daughters for the widow and two sons for her, each with betrothal gifts of a thousand gold.
translations.idiomatic: Over twenty years he amassed a fortune, married off three daughters and found wives for two sons, each match sealed with betrothal gifts worth a thousand gold.

sentences.zh: 又延師教二子，輸粟為太學生。

translations.literal: He also engaged teachers to instruct the two sons and paid grain tribute so they could become imperial academy students.
translations.idiomatic: He hired tutors for the two sons and paid tribute grain to enroll them in the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 自是，寡婦財雄一邑。

translations.literal: From then on the widow's wealth dominated the whole county.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the widow was the wealthiest person in the county.

sentences.zh: 及寄病且死，謂寡婦曰：「老奴牛馬之報盡矣。

translations.literal: When Ji grew ill and was near death, he told the widow: "This old servant's repayment in the manner of ox and horse is finished."
translations.idiomatic: When Ji fell mortally ill, he told the widow, "I have repaid my debt to you, like an ox or a horse, down to the last."

sentences.zh: 」出枕中二籍，則家鉅細悉均分之，曰：「以此遺兩郎君，可世守也。

translations.literal: He took out two ledgers from beneath his pillow in which every great and small item of the household was equally divided, saying: "With this bequeath to the two young masters—they may guard it through generations."
translations.idiomatic: He drew two ledgers from under his pillow, dividing every asset equally, and said, "Leave these to the two young masters. They can preserve the family for generations."

sentences.zh: 」既歿，或疑其有私，竊啟其篋，無一金蓄。

translations.literal: After he died, some suspected he had kept something private; they secretly opened his chest and found not a single coin saved.
translations.idiomatic: After his death some suspected he had hoarded a private store. They opened his chest in secret and found not a single coin.

sentences.zh: 所遺一嫗一兒，僅敝缊掩體而已。

translations.literal: What he left was one old woman and one child, barely covered in worn rags—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: All he left behind was an old woman and a child, barely clothed in patched rags.

sentences.zh: 趙重華，雲南太和人。

translations.literal: Zhao Chonghua was a man of Taihe in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chonghua was from Taihe in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 七歲時，父廷瑞遊江湖間，久不返。

translations.literal: When he was seven, his father Tingrui traveled among rivers and lakes and long did not return.
translations.idiomatic: When he was seven, his father Tingrui went wandering and did not return for many years.

sentences.zh: 重華長，謁郡守請路引，榜其背曰：「萬里尋親。

translations.literal: When Chonghua grew up, he visited the prefect and requested a travel permit; on his back was posted a placard reading: "Seeking kin for ten thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, he petitioned the prefect for a travel permit. A placard on his back read, "Searching for my father across ten thousand li."

sentences.zh: 」別書父年貌、邑里數千紙，所歷都會州縣遍張之。

translations.literal: Separately he wrote his father's age, appearance, and native place on thousands of sheets and posted them everywhere in every metropolis and county he passed.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his father's age, appearance, and hometown on thousands of notices and posted them in every city and county he passed through.

sentences.zh: 西禱武當山，經太子巖，巖陰有字曰：「嘉靖四十四年十二月十二日，趙廷瑞朝山至此。

translations.literal: Traveling west he prayed at Wudang Mountain; passing Taizi Cliff, on the shaded face of the cliff were characters reading: "Jiajing 44, twelfth month, twelfth day—Zhao Tingrui came here on pilgrimage."
translations.idiomatic: He traveled west to pray at Wudang Mountain. At Taizi Cliff he found an inscription in the shade: "On the twelfth day of the twelfth month of Jiajing 44, Zhao Tingrui came here on pilgrimage."

sentences.zh: 」重華讀之，慟曰：「吾父果過此，今吾之來月日正同，可卜相逢矣。

translations.literal: Chonghua read it and grieved, saying: "My father did indeed pass here; today my month and day of arrival are exactly the same—surely this foretells we shall meet."
translations.idiomatic: Reading it, Chonghua wept and said, "My father did pass this way—and today is the same month and day he came. Surely we will meet."

sentences.zh: 」遂書其後曰：「萬歷六年十二月十二日，趙廷瑞之子重華，尋父至此。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wrote afterward: "Wanli 6, twelfth month, twelfth day—Zhao Tingrui's son Chonghua, seeking his father, arrived here."
translations.idiomatic: He added beneath it: "On the twelfth day of the twelfth month of Wanli 6, Zhao Tingrui's son Chonghua came here searching for his father."

sentences.zh: 」久之竟無所遇。

translations.literal: After a long time he still met with nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, after long searching, he found no trace of his father.

sentences.zh: 過丹陽，盜攫其資，所遺獨路引。

translations.literal: Passing Danyang, bandits seized his funds; all that remained was the travel permit.
translations.idiomatic: At Danyang, robbers took everything he had. Only his travel permit was left.

sentences.zh: 且行且乞，遇一老僧呼問其故，笑曰：「汝父客無錫南禪寺中。

translations.literal: Traveling and begging as he went, he met an old monk who called to him and asked his reason; the monk smiled and said: "Your father is staying as a guest at Nanchan Temple in Wuxi."
translations.idiomatic: He went on begging as he traveled. An old monk called to him, asked his story, and smiled: "Your father is lodging at Nanchan Temple in Wuxi."

sentences.zh: 」語訖忽不見。

translations.literal: When the words were finished he suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: The words had barely left his lips when the monk vanished.

sentences.zh: 重華急趨至寺，果其父，出路引示之，相與慟哭。

translations.literal: Chonghua hastened to the temple and found indeed his father; he produced the travel permit to show him, and together they wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua ran to the temple and found his father. He showed him the travel permit, and they wept in each other's arms.

sentences.zh: 留數日，乃還雲南。

translations.literal: He stayed several days, then returned to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: After a few days together, they returned to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 是時，有謝廣者，祁門人。

translations.literal: At this time there was one Xie Guang, a man of Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time there was Xie Guang of Qimen.

sentences.zh: 父求仙不返，廣娶婦七日即別母求父，遇於開封逆旅中。

translations.literal: His father went seeking immortals and did not return; Guang married and after seven days parted from his mother to seek his father, meeting him at an inn in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: His father had gone in search of immortals and never returned. Guang married, and seven days later left his mother to find his father. They met at an inn in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父乘間復脫去。

translations.literal: His father seized an opportunity and slipped away again.
translations.idiomatic: His father seized a moment and slipped away again.

sentences.zh: 廣跋涉四方者垂二十年，終不得父，聞者哀之。

translations.literal: Guang wandered the four quarters for nearly twenty years and in the end never found his father; those who heard it mourned for him.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly twenty years he wandered the country, never finding his father again. All who heard his story grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 王世名，字時望，武義人。

translations.literal: Wang Shiming, courtesy name Shiwang, was a man of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiming, styled Shiwang, was from Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 父良，與族子俊同居爭屋，為俊毆死。

translations.literal: His father Liang lived with clansman Jun and quarreled over the house; Jun beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liang shared a house with a clansman named Jun. They quarreled over the property, and Jun beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 世名年十七，恐殘父屍，不忍就理，乃佯聽其輸田議和。

translations.literal: Shiming was seventeen; fearing his father's corpse would be mutilated, he could not bear to pursue justice, and so pretended to accept Jun's offer of land in settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Shiming was seventeen. Fearing his father's body would be desecrated, he could not bring himself to press his case in court. Instead he pretended to accept Jun's offer of land as settlement.

sentences.zh: 凡田所入，輒易價封識。

translations.literal: Whatever income the fields yielded, he immediately exchanged for cash and sealed and marked it.
translations.idiomatic: Every penny from the fields he exchanged for cash, sealed and marked for safekeeping.

sentences.zh: 俊有所饋，亦佯受之。

translations.literal: Whenever Jun made gifts, he also pretended to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Jun offered him, he pretended to accept graciously.

sentences.zh: 而潛繪父像懸密室，繪己像於旁，帶刀侍，朝夕泣拜，且購一刃，銘「報仇」二字，母妻不知也。

translations.literal: Yet secretly he painted his father's portrait and hung it in a hidden room, painted his own likeness beside it with sword in hand attending; morning and evening he wept and bowed, and moreover bought a blade inscribed with the two characters "Avenge," of which mother and wife knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he painted his father's portrait and hung it in a hidden room, with his own likeness beside it, sword in hand, standing watch. Morning and evening he wept and bowed before it. He bought a blade engraved with the word "Vengeance." His mother and wife knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為諸生。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he became a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he enrolled as a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 及生子數月，謂母妻曰：「吾已有後，可以死矣。

translations.literal: When his son was several months old, he told mother and wife: "I already have an heir—I can die now."
translations.idiomatic: When his son was a few months old, he told his mother and wife, "I have an heir now. I can die."

sentences.zh: 」一日，俊自外醉歸，世名挺刃迎擊之，立斃。

translations.literal: One day Jun returned drunk from outside; Shiming drew his blade and met him in attack, killing him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: One day Jun came home drunk. Shiming met him with his blade and killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 出號於眾，入白母，即取前封識者詣吏請死。

translations.literal: He raised a cry among the crowd, went in to tell his mother, then took the previously sealed and marked goods to the magistrate and asked for death.
translations.idiomatic: He cried out to the crowd, told his mother, then took the sealed cash to the magistrate and offered himself for execution.

sentences.zh: 時萬歷九年二月，去父死六年矣。

translations.literal: It was the second month of Wanli 9, six years since his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: It was the second month of Wanli 9—six years after his father's murder.

sentences.zh: 知縣陳某曰：「此孝子也，不可置獄。

translations.literal: Magistrate Chen said: "This is a filial son—he must not be put in prison."
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Chen said, "This is a filial son. He must not be jailed."

sentences.zh: 」別館之，而上其事於府。

translations.literal: He lodged him separately and reported the matter upward to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He housed him separately and reported the case to the prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 府檄金華知縣汪大受來訊。

translations.literal: The prefecture issued a dispatch ordering Jinhua Magistrate Wang Dashou to come and conduct the inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture ordered Jinhua Magistrate Wang Dashou to investigate.

sentences.zh: 世名請死，大受曰：「檢屍有傷，爾可無死。

translations.literal: Shiming asked for death; Dashou said: "If the corpse examination shows wounds, you need not die."
translations.idiomatic: Shiming asked to die. Dashou said, "If the autopsy confirms the wounds, you won't have to die."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「吾惟不忍殘父屍，以至今日。

translations.literal: He said: "It was only because I could not bear to mutilate my father's corpse that things reached today."
translations.idiomatic: Shiming replied, "It was only because I could not bear to have my father's body desecrated that I waited until today."

sentences.zh: 不然，何待六年。

translations.literal: Otherwise, why wait six years?"
translations.idiomatic: "Otherwise, why would I have waited six years?"

sentences.zh: 乞放歸辭母乃就死。

translations.literal: He begged to be released to take leave of his mother before accepting death.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to go home first to bid his mother farewell before dying.

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 歸，母迎而泣。

translations.literal: Returning home, his mother came to meet him weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, his mother met him in tears.

sentences.zh: 世名曰：「身者，父之遺也。

translations.literal: Shiming said: "The body is what one's father bequeaths."
translations.idiomatic: Shiming said, "My body is my father's legacy."

sentences.zh: 以父之遺為父死，雖離母，得從父矣，何憾。

translations.literal: To use what one's father bequeathed to die for one's father—though parted from mother, one may follow father; what regret is there?"
translations.idiomatic: "To use my father's gift to die for my father—even if I must leave my mother, I go to my father. What regret could I have?"

sentences.zh: 」頃之，大受至，縣人奔走直世名者以千計。

translations.literal: Shortly Dashou arrived; people of the county who came straight to Shiming numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Dashou arrived. Thousands of county residents converged on Shiming's home.

sentences.zh: 大受乃令人舁致父棺，將開視之。

translations.literal: Dashou then had men carry his father's coffin over, intending to open it for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou ordered Shiming's father's coffin brought forth and opened for examination.

sentences.zh: 世名大慟，以頭觸階石，血流殷地。

translations.literal: Shiming grieved greatly, struck his head against the step stone, and blood flowed copiously on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Shiming was overcome with grief. He dashed his head against the stone steps until blood pooled on the ground.

sentences.zh: 大受及旁觀者鹹為隕涕，乃令舁柩去，將白上官免檢屍，以全孝子。

translations.literal: Dashou and onlookers all shed tears; then he ordered the coffin carried away, intending to report upward to exempt the corpse examination and preserve the filial son.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou and all who watched wept. He ordered the coffin taken away and planned to petition his superiors to waive the autopsy, to preserve the filial son's honor.

sentences.zh: 世名曰：「此非法也，非法無君，何以生為。

translations.literal: Shiming said: "This is not according to law; without law there is no ruler—what point is there in living?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiming said, "That would violate the law. Without law there is no sovereign. What point would there be in living?"

sentences.zh: 」遂不食而死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stopped eating and died.
translations.idiomatic: He refused food and starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 妻俞氏，撫孤三載，自縊以殉，旌其門曰孝烈。

translations.literal: His wife, née Yu, nurtured the orphan for three years, then hanged herself to follow him in death; their gate was commended as "Filial and Resolute."
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Yu, raised their child for three years, then hanged herself to join him. Their household was commended with the title "Filial and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 李文詠，昆山諸生。

translations.literal: Li Wenyong was a licentiate of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenyong was a student of Kunshan who held licentiate status.

sentences.zh: 父大經，沂水知縣。

translations.literal: His father Dajing was magistrate of Yishui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dajing was magistrate of Yishui County.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十七年，父寢室被火。

translations.literal: In Wanli 27 his father's bedchamber caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 27, fire broke out in his father's bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 文詠突入，將父抱出，而榱棟盡覆，父子俱焚死。

translations.literal: Wenyong rushed in and was about to carry his father out, but rafters and beams all collapsed; father and son both perished in the flames.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyong rushed in to carry his father out, but the roof collapsed. Father and son were burned alive.

sentences.zh: 火息，入視，屍猶覆其父，父存全體，文詠但余一股。

translations.literal: When the fire subsided, upon entering to look, the corpse still covered his father; the father remained whole in body, while Wenyong had only one leg left.
translations.idiomatic: When the fire died down, they found Wenyong's body still shielding his father. His father was intact; of Wenyong, only one leg remained.

sentences.zh: 王應元，武隆人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuanyuan was a man of Wulong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanyuan was from Wulong.

sentences.zh: 力農養父。

translations.literal: He labored at farming to support his father.
translations.idiomatic: He worked the fields to support his father.

sentences.zh: 父醉臥，家失火。

translations.literal: His father lay drunk asleep when the house caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: His father was drunk and asleep when fire broke out in the house.

sentences.zh: 應元自外趨烈焰中，竟不能出，抱父死。

translations.literal: Yuanyuan from outside rushed into the flames; in the end he could not get out and died embracing his father.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyuan ran from outside into the blaze. He never came out—he died holding his father.

sentences.zh: 唐治，黃岡人。

translations.literal: Tang Zhi was a man of Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhi was from Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 父柩在堂，鄰居火，治盡出資財募人舁柩，人各自顧，無應者。

translations.literal: His father's coffin was in the hall; a neighbor's fire broke out; Zhi spent all his goods to hire men to move the coffin, but everyone looked to himself and none responded.
translations.idiomatic: His father's coffin lay in the hall when a neighbor's house caught fire. Tang Zhi offered all he had to hire men to move the coffin, but everyone looked to their own safety and no one came.

sentences.zh: 或挽之出，泣曰：「父柩在此，我死不出。

translations.literal: Some tried to pull him out; weeping he said: "My father's coffin is here—I will not leave even if I die."
translations.idiomatic: Some tried to drag him out. Weeping, he said, "My father's coffin is here. I will not leave, even if I die."

sentences.zh: 」火息，後堂巋然獨存，柩亦無恙，而治竟熏灼伏柩死。

translations.literal: When the fire died down, the rear hall alone stood intact, the coffin unharmed; yet Zhi in the end was burned to death lying over the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When the fire subsided, the rear hall alone stood intact and the coffin was unharmed—but Zhi had burned to death shielding it.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中旌表。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he received official commendation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he received official commendation.

sentences.zh: 許恩，蘄水人。

translations.literal: Xu En was a man of Qishui.
translations.idiomatic: Xu En was from Qishui.

sentences.zh: 夜半鄰家失火，恩驚出，遍尋母不得，復突入，遂與母俱焚。

translations.literal: At midnight a neighbor's house caught fire; En rushed out in alarm, searched everywhere but could not find his mother, then burst back in, and perished with her in the flames.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight a neighbor's house caught fire. En rushed out in alarm and searched everywhere but could not find his mother. He burst back in and perished with her in the flames.

sentences.zh: 馮象臨，慈谿諸生。

translations.literal: Feng Xianglin was a licentiate of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xianglin was a student of Cixi who held licentiate status.

sentences.zh: 家被火，遍覓父母，煙焰彌空，迷失庭戶。

translations.literal: When his house caught fire, he searched everywhere for his parents; smoke and flames filled the sky, and he lost his way among the halls and doors.
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out in his home, he searched everywhere for his parents. Smoke and flames filled the sky and he lost his way among the rooms.

sentences.zh: 象臨大呼，初得母，即從火中負出。

translations.literal: Xianglin cried out loudly; having first found his mother, he immediately carried her out from the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Xianglin shouted loudly. Once he found his mother, he carried her out through the flames.

sentences.zh: 再入負父，並挾一弟以出，半體已焦爛。

translations.literal: Entering again he carried out his father, bringing along a younger brother as well; half his body was already charred and burned.
translations.idiomatic: He went back in, carried out his father, and brought out a younger brother as well. Half his body was already charred.

sentences.zh: 聞妹尚留臥內，母號呼，將自入，亟止之，觸烈焰攜妹出，竟灼爛而死。

translations.literal: Hearing his sister still remained in the bedroom, his mother wailed and was about to enter herself; he urgently stopped her, plunged through the flames to bring his sister out, and in the end was burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing his sister was still inside, his mother wailed and tried to go back in. He stopped her, plunged through the flames, and brought his sister out—but was burned to death.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜旌。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, commendation was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the story became known, the court granted official commendation.

sentences.zh: 後有龔作梅者，陳州人。

translations.literal: Later there was one Gong Zuomei, a man of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was Gong Zuomei of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 年十七，父母俱亡，殯於舍。

translations.literal: At seventeen, both parents had died and lay in coffins in the house.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, both his parents had died. Their coffins lay in the house.

sentences.zh: 闖賊火民居，作梅跪柩前焚死。

translations.literal: Bandits set fire to a residence; Zuomei knelt before the coffins and burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits torched a house. Zuomei knelt before the coffins and burned to death.

sentences.zh: 孔金，山陽人。

translations.literal: Kong Jin was a man of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jin was from Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 父早亡，母謝氏，遺腹三月而生金。

translations.literal: His father died early; his mother was surnamed Xie; three months after his death she bore Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His father died young. His mother, Lady Xie, was three months pregnant when he died and bore Jin thereafter.

sentences.zh: 母為大賈杜言逼娶，投河死。

translations.literal: His mother was forced to marry by the great merchant Du Yan and drowned herself in the river.
translations.idiomatic: The great merchant Du Yan forced his mother to marry him. She drowned herself in the river.

sentences.zh: 金長，屢訟於官，不勝。

translations.literal: When Jin grew up, he repeatedly sued in court but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin came of age, he sued again and again in court but never won.

sentences.zh: 言行賄欲斃金，金乃乞食走闕下，擊登聞鼓訴冤，不得達。

translations.literal: Yan tried to bribe officials to have Jin killed; Jin then begged for food and fled to the capital, struck the drum for appeals at the palace gate to proclaim his grievance, but could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: Yan bribed officials to have Jin killed. Jin begged his way to the capital and beat the appeal drum at the palace gate, but his petition never reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 還墓所，晝夜號泣。

translations.literal: Returning to the grave site, he wailed day and night.
