translations.idiomatic: He returned to his mother's grave and wailed day and night.

sentences.zh: 裏人劉清等陳其事於府，知府張守約異之，召閭族媒氏質實，坐言大辟。

translations.literal: Villagers Liu Qing and others reported the matter to the prefecture; Prefect Zhang Shouyue was astonished, summoned neighborhood, clan, and matchmaker to verify the facts, and sentenced Yan to capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers including Liu Qing reported the case to the prefecture. Prefect Zhang Shouyue was struck by it. He summoned neighbors, clansmen, and the matchmaker to verify the facts and sentenced Yan to death.

sentences.zh: 未幾守約卒，言夤緣免。

translations.literal: Before long Shouyue died, and Yan used connections to escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shouyue died, and Yan used connections to escape the sentence.

sentences.zh: 金復號訴不已，被箠無完膚。

translations.literal: Jin again cried out and petitioned without cease, was beaten until not an inch of skin was whole.
translations.idiomatic: Jin kept crying out and petitioning without cease. He was beaten until his body was a mass of wounds.

sentences.zh: 已而撫按理舊牘，仍坐言大辟，迄死獄中。

translations.literal: Before long the grand coordinator reviewed old documents, again sentenced Yan to capital punishment, and he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually the grand coordinator reviewed the old files, again sentenced Yan to death, and Yan died in prison.

sentences.zh: 金子良亦有孝行，父病，刲股為羹以進，旋愈。

translations.literal: Jin's son Liang also had filial conduct; when his father was ill, he cut flesh from his thigh to make broth and presented it, and soon he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's son Liang was also filial. When his father fell ill, he cut flesh from his thigh, made broth, and fed it to him. His father soon recovered.

sentences.zh: 比卒，廬墓哀毀。

translations.literal: When he died, he lived in a hut by the tomb in grief and emaciation.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he mourned at the grave in a hut, wasting away in grief.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十三年，父子並得旌。

translations.literal: In Wanli 43 both father and son received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 43, father and son both received official commendation.

sentences.zh: 楊通照、通傑，銅仁人。

translations.literal: Yang Tongzhao and Tongjie were men of Tongren.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tongzhao and Tongjie were from Tongren.

sentences.zh: 母周氏有疾，兄弟爭拜禱，求以身代。

translations.literal: Their mother, née Zhou, was ill; the brothers vied in bowing and praying, each asking to substitute his own body for hers.
translations.idiomatic: Their mother, Lady Zhou, fell ill. The brothers competed in prayer, each begging to suffer in her place.

sentences.zh: 閱三年，不入內室。

translations.literal: For three years they did not enter the inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: For three years they did not enter the inner chambers of the house.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十六年，群苗流劫，至其家，母被執去。

translations.literal: In Wanli 36 bandits from various Miao groups swept through in plunder; reaching their home, they seized the mother and took her away.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 36, Miao raiders swept through the region. They reached the brothers' home and seized their mother.

sentences.zh: 二人追鬥數十里，被傷不顧。

translations.literal: The two pursued and fought for dozens of li, ignoring their wounds.
translations.idiomatic: The two brothers pursued them for dozens of li, ignoring their wounds.

sentences.zh: 至鬼空溪，見賊縶母，大罵，聲震山谷，橫擊萬眾中，為賊所磔死。

translations.literal: Reaching Guikong Stream, they saw the bandits holding their mother bound; they cursed loudly, their voices shaking the valleys, and charged across among ten thousand men; both were dismembered and killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At Guikong Stream they found the bandits holding their mother captive. They cursed until their voices shook the valleys and charged into the midst of the enemy host. The bandits dismembered and killed them both.

sentences.zh: 通照年二十五，通傑年二十二。

translations.literal: Tongzhao was twenty-five, Tongjie twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhao was twenty-five; Tongjie was twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 泰昌元年，巡撫李枟、巡按史永安上其事，旌曰雙孝之門。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang, Grand Coordinator Li Yin and Regional Inspector Shi Yong'an reported the matter upward; their gate was commended as "Gate of Twin Filial Piety."
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang 1, Grand Coordinator Li Yin and Regional Inspector Shi Yong'an reported the case. Their household was commended with the title "Gate of Twin Filial Piety."

sentences.zh: 時無錫民浦邵，賊縛其父虞，將殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Pu Shao, a commoner of Wuxi, had bandits bind his father Yu and mean to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pu Shao, a commoner of Wuxi, had bandits bind his father Yu and prepare to kill him.

sentences.zh: 邵以首迎刃而死，父得免。

translations.literal: Shao offered his neck to the blade and died; his father was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Shao put his neck to the blade and died. His father was spared.

sentences.zh: 寧化民林上元，賊掠其繼母李氏出城，上元從城上持槍一躍而下，直奔賊壘，刺死二人。

translations.literal: Lin Shangyuan, a commoner of Ninghua, had bandits carry off his stepmother, née Li, outside the city; Shangyuan leaped down from the wall holding a spear, dashed straight into the bandit camp, and stabbed two men to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shangyuan, a commoner of Ninghua, had bandits carry off his stepmother, Lady Li, outside the city walls. He leaped from the wall with a spear, charged straight into the bandit camp, and killed two men.

sentences.zh: 賊避其鋒，立出李氏，因引去，城賴以全。

translations.literal: The bandits avoided his thrust, immediately released Li, and then withdrew; the city was preserved thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits fell back before his assault, released Lady Li, and withdrew. The city was saved.

sentences.zh: 皆萬歷四十三年旌。

translations.literal: All received commendation in Wanli 43.
translations.idiomatic: All received official commendation in Wanli 43.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年，流賊陷竹谿，執知縣余霄將殺之。

translations.literal: In Chongzhen 7 rebel bandits took Zhuxi, seized Magistrate Yu Xiao, and meant to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 7, rebel bandits captured Zhuxi, seized Magistrate Yu Xiao, and prepared to execute him.

sentences.zh: 子諸生伯麟請代，乃免。

translations.literal: His son, licentiate Bolin, asked to take his place, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bolin, a licentiate, offered to die in his place, and the magistrate was spared.

sentences.zh: 張清雅，潛山人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qingya was a man of Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qingya was from Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 家貧，力學養親。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he studied diligently to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor. He studied hard to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年，張獻忠來犯。

translations.literal: In Chongzhen 10 Zhang Xianzhong came to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 10, Zhang Xianzhong's forces attacked.

sentences.zh: 清雅以父年老臥病，守之不去。

translations.literal: Qingya, because his father was old and bedridden with illness, stayed to guard him and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Qingya's father was old and bedridden. He stayed to guard him and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 無何，父卒。

translations.literal: Before long his father died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his father died.

sentences.zh: 斂甫畢，賊入其家，疑棺內藏金銀，欲剖視之。

translations.literal: Just as the encoffining was completed, bandits entered his home, suspecting gold and silver hidden in the coffin, and meant to open it for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the encoffining was finished, bandits entered the house. Suspecting gold and silver in the coffin, they meant to open it.

sentences.zh: 清雅據棺哀泣，賊斷其手，仆地。

translations.literal: Qingya clung to the coffin weeping in grief; the bandits severed his hand and he fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Qingya clung to the coffin and wept. The bandits cut off his hand and he collapsed.

sentences.zh: 幼子超藝年十六，號哭求代。

translations.literal: His younger son Chaoyi, aged sixteen, wailed and begged to take his place.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Chaoyi, sixteen, wailed and begged to die in his father's place.

sentences.zh: 賊復砍之，父子俱死，而棺得不剖。

translations.literal: The bandits again hacked at him; father and son both died, yet the coffin was not opened.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits hacked at him too. Father and son both died, but the coffin was never opened.

sentences.zh: 仆雲滿，具兩棺斂之，亦不食死。

translations.literal: The servant Yunman prepared two coffins to bury them and also died by refusing food.
translations.idiomatic: The servant Yunman prepared two coffins for them and starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 時有白精忠者，潁州人。

translations.literal: At that time there was one Bai Jingzhong, a man of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was Bai Jingzhong of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 五歲而孤，母袁氏撫之。

translations.literal: Orphaned at five, his mother, née Yuan, raised him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at five, he was raised by his mother, Lady Yuan.

sentences.zh: 家貧，母食糠核，而以精者哺兒。

translations.literal: The family was poor; his mother ate chaff and husks and fed the finer grains to her son.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor. His mother ate chaff and husks and saved the better food for her son.

sentences.zh: 精忠知之，每餐必先啖其惡者。

translations.literal: Jingzhong knew this; at every meal he always ate the worse portion first.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong knew this. At every meal he ate the worst portion first.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，舉於鄉。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年，流賊陷潁州，家人勸逃匿。

translations.literal: In Chongzhen 8 rebel bandits took Yingzhou; his family urged him to flee and hide.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 8, rebel bandits captured Yingzhou. His family urged him to flee.

sentences.zh: 精忠以母年老，不忍獨去，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Jingzhong, because his mother was old, could not bear to leave alone, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong's mother was old; he could not bear to flee alone and was killed.

sentences.zh: 州有檀之槐者，護母柩下去。

translations.literal: In the prefecture there was one Tan Zhihuai, who guarded his mother's coffin as he fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefecture was Tan Zhihuai, who fled while guarding his mother's coffin.

sentences.zh: 與賊格鬥，殺數人，被磔死。

translations.literal: He fought the bandits hand to hand, killed several men, and was dismembered and killed.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the bandits, killed several men, and was dismembered and killed.

sentences.zh: 又有李心唯，素敦孝行。

translations.literal: There was also Li Xinwei, who from of old esteemed filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Li Xinwei, known for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 賊至，泣守母喪。

translations.literal: When bandits arrived, he wept as he kept vigil over his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits arrived, he wept as he kept vigil over his mother's funeral.

sentences.zh: 賊掠其室，將縛之，不出，被殺。

translations.literal: Bandits plundered his house and meant to bind him; he would not come out and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits looted his house and tried to bind him. He refused to come out and was killed.

sentences.zh: 子果，見父死，厲聲罵賊，賊又殺之。

translations.literal: His son Guo, seeing his father dead, cursed the bandits in a loud voice; the bandits killed him too.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guo saw his father dead and cursed the bandits at the top of his lungs. They killed him too.

sentences.zh: 有余承德者，無為人。

translations.literal: There was one Yu Chengde, a man of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: There was Yu Chengde of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十五年，流賊突至，掖其祖母劉氏、母魏氏及妻楊氏、妹玉女出避。

translations.literal: In Chongzhen 15 rebel bandits suddenly arrived; he supported his grandmother, née Liu, his mother, née Wei, his wife, née Yang, and his sister Yunu as they fled.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 15, rebel bandits suddenly arrived. He helped his grandmother Lady Liu, his mother Lady Wei, his wife Lady Yang, and his sister Yunu flee.

sentences.zh: 祖母、母行遲，為盜所獲，欲刃之。

translations.literal: Grandmother and mother walked slowly and were seized by robbers, who meant to cut them down with blades.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother and mother could not keep up. Robbers seized them and raised their blades.

sentences.zh: 承德號呼救護，並遇害。

translations.literal: Chengde cried out calling for help to protect them and was killed along with them.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde cried out and rushed to protect them. He was killed along with them.

sentences.zh: 楊氏見之，急投河死。

translations.literal: Yang, seeing this, hastily threw herself into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang saw it and threw herself into the river.

sentences.zh: 賊將犯玉女，玉女大罵，堅不從，寸磔而死。

translations.literal: The bandits meant to violate Yunu; Yunu cursed loudly, firmly refusing, and was dismembered inch by inch to death.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits meant to violate Yunu. She cursed them and firmly refused. They dismembered her inch by inch.
